stories.what_happened: Godrej Consumer Products announced that Managing Director and CEO **Sudhir Sitapati** has resigned, with Chief Financial Officer **Aasif Malbari** stepping in as his replacement effective **August 12, 2026**. The stock reacted immediately and sharply: GCPL shares dropped as much as **10.6%** intraday — their steepest fall since December 2024 — as investors were caught off guard by the abruptness of the departure. The broader market was largely unaffected: the **Sensex gained around 109 points** the same day, showing this was a company-specific shock rather than a sector-wide selloff, though peer stock HUL also dipped slightly in sympathy.
key_points: Godrej Consumer Products (GCPL) shares fell as much as **10.6%**, the steepest drop since **December 2024**.
CEO and Managing Director **Sudhir Sitapati** resigned effective **August 12**.
CFO **Aasif Malbari** has stepped in as his replacement.
The sudden, unexplained exit **spooked investors** already wary of India's slowing FMCG sector.
The wider Sensex actually **rose ~109 points** the same day, showing this was a company-specific shock.

depth.background: Godrej Consumer Products is one of India's biggest household-and-personal-care companies, selling soaps, hair color and insecticides under brands like Godrej and Good Knight. **Sudhir Sitapati** took over as CEO in 2022 after a well-regarded run at Hindustan Unilever, and was widely seen as steering the company's growth strategy. India's FMCG (fast-moving consumer goods) stocks have already been under pressure this year from slowing urban consumption and margin pressure.

stories.title: A record 231-run stand powers Afghanistan to a series-sealing 42-run win over Ireland
stories.what_happened: Afghanistan posted a commanding **343 for 9** in the 4th ODI at Belfast's Civil Service Cricket Club, anchored by a **231-run partnership** between **Ibrahim Zadran** and **Sediqullah Atal** — the highest second-wicket stand in Afghanistan's ODI history. Atal top-scored with **143 off 120 balls** and was named Player of the Match, while Ireland's McDonough (3 for 84) and Hoey (2 for 71) did what damage they could. Chasing 344, Ireland put up a real fight through half-centuries from **Andy Balbirnie (109)** and Curtis Campher (84), but fell 42 runs short, finishing on 301. Afghanistan's bowlers, led by **Yamin Ahmadzai (4 for 71)** and spin great **Rashid Khan (3 for 49)**, closed out the win. The result gives Afghanistan an **unassailable 3-0 lead** in the five-match series, with the fifth and final ODI still to come.
key_points: Afghanistan beat Ireland by **42 runs** in the 4th ODI in Belfast, posting **343 for 9**.
**Ibrahim Zadran and Sediqullah Atal put on 231 runs** together — Afghanistan's highest-ever 2nd-wicket stand in ODIs.
**Sediqullah Atal scored 143** off 120 balls and was named Player of the Match.
Ireland fought back with **Andy Balbirnie (109)** and Curtis Campher (84), but fell short chasing 344.
The win gives Afghanistan an **unassailable 3-0 lead** in the five-match series, with one game left to play.

depth.background: Afghanistan's cricket team has become one of the format's most dangerous white-ball sides in recent years, built around explosive batting and world-class spin from players like Rashid Khan. This series in Ireland matters beyond bragging rights: Afghanistan had already used an earlier win in the series to lock in a direct qualification spot for the 2027 ODI Cricket World Cup, so these later matches are as much about form and momentum as they are about the series scoreline itself.

thread.previously: We reported Afghanistan had already secured a direct spot at the 2027 Cricket World Cup by beating Ireland in their ongoing ODI series.
thread.changed: Afghanistan has now won the 4th ODI too, by 42 runs, built on a record 231-run partnership between Ibrahim Zadran and Sediqullah Atal — extending their lead to an unassailable 3-0 with one match left.

stories.title: BCCI scraps the A+ grade and demotes Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli to Grade B in new central contracts
stories.what_happened: The BCCI finalized its central contracts for the **2026-27 season**, and the changes were significant: the **A+ grade has been scrapped altogether**, and the new top Grade A now includes just **three players** — captain-calibre all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja, fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah, and India's Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli, both previously in the A+ bracket, have been **moved down to Grade B**, reflecting that they're now limited to the 50-over format. Elsewhere in the list, all-rounder Washington Sundar was bumped up from Grade C to B, while Sai Sudharsan — who made his Test debut last year — received his first-ever central contract, at Grade C. Fast bowler Mohammed Shami reportedly dropped out of the contracted list entirely.
key_points: The BCCI's **A+ category, its top tier since 2018**, has been scrapped entirely.
Only **three players** — Shubman Gill, Jasprit Bumrah, and Ravindra Jadeja — now hold the new top Grade A.
**Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli have been demoted** from A+ to Grade B.
The demotion reflects that both now play **only ODIs**, having retired from Tests and T20Is.
Washington Sundar was **promoted from C to B**; Sai Sudharsan received his first contract, at Grade C.

depth.background: The BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India) pays its contracted players annual retainers split into grades — historically A+, A, B, and C — largely based on how many formats a player plays and their importance to the team. The A+ tier was introduced in 2018 specifically to reward India's most indispensable multi-format stars with the highest pay. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli, two of India's greatest modern batters, have already retired from Test cricket and T20Is over the past year, meaning they now represent India only in ODIs (One Day Internationals).

stories.title: FIA admits its ADUO engine catch-up system has 'weaknesses' as Red Bull dispute rankings
stories.what_happened: The FIA's first ADUO assessment of the 2026 season ranked **Red Bull Ford Powertrains** as the benchmark engine, the one every rival is measured against — which means Red Bull itself gets **zero bonus upgrade tokens** while Mercedes, Ferrari and others qualify for extra development. Red Bull immediately pushed back, arguing its own trackside data shows no clear power advantage over Mercedes, and requested a formal FIA review. Speaking to reporters, Tombazis defended the accuracy of the FIA's measurements but conceded the process is **'quite sensitive'** and has weaknesses worth fixing — chiefly that scoring only the combustion engine while ignoring the hybrid electric system can produce a ranking that doesn't match what's actually fastest on track. Separately, **Toto Wolff** has said Mercedes now believes it has the most powerful engine on the grid, a claim Red Bull does not strongly dispute — deepening the contradiction between the official ADUO ranking and the on-track picture. The FIA has spent over a week re-examining the data before confirming the rankings and upgrade allocations.
key_points: FIA single-seater director **Nikolas Tombazis** admitted the ADUO system 'is working as it was designed' but has **'some weaknesses that we need to address in the future.'**
The system ranks engines using only the **internal combustion engine (ICE)** output, ignoring the electric **ERS** system that makes up roughly **50%** of a 2026 power unit's total performance.
**Red Bull Ford Powertrains** was placed top of the initial rankings, meaning it is the **only manufacturer denied bonus upgrade tokens** under the rule.
Red Bull has publicly challenged the verdict, arguing **'no data sample indicates an advantage over Mercedes'** on track.
Rivals could theoretically **withhold upgrade tokens** to keep Red Bull stuck at the top of the ranking indefinitely, a loophole Tombazis has acknowledged but downplayed.

depth.background: F1's all-new **2026 hybrid engine rules** roughly doubled the electric power contribution from the battery/motor system, drawing in new manufacturers like **Audi** and a reworked **Honda** partnership with Aston Martin. To stop one manufacturer running away with an engine advantage, the FIA built in a mid-season catch-up mechanism called **ADUO** ('Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities'): any manufacturer measured **2-4% behind** the best engine gets one bonus upgrade, and anyone **more than 4%** behind gets two. The rule was designed with manufacturers' own input in 2025, who reportedly asked the FIA to keep the measurement simple.

stories.title: North Korea fires second ballistic missile in a week, days before US-South Korea drills
stories.what_happened: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said North Korea fired a suspected ballistic missile from the Wonsan area on its eastern coast around 6 a.m. local time on Wednesday. The missile flew more than 700 kilometers before coming down in the sea between the Korean Peninsula and Japan. Japan's Defense Ministry detected the launch too and said it appeared to land outside Japan's exclusive economic zone, an area extending 200 nautical miles from its coast. This was North Korea's second missile launch in under a week, following a short-range ballistic missile test on August 6 that was also detected jointly by South Korea, the US and Japan. The new test came just two days after Seoul and Washington announced their annual large-scale joint military exercises would begin on August 17.
key_points: North Korea launched a **ballistic missile** from its eastern Wonsan coast around **6 a.m.** local time on Wednesday, which flew more than **700 kilometers (435 miles)** before landing in the sea.
It's North Korea's **second** missile test in **less than a week** — the first came on August 6.
The launch comes two days after South Korea and the US announced their **annual joint military drills** will begin August 17, which Pyongyang calls a rehearsal for invasion.
South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff and National Security Council condemned the launch as an **'act of provocation'** and said the South remains ready to respond alongside the US.
Japan's Defense Ministry said the missile appears to have landed **outside** its exclusive economic zone; Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi called the pattern of launches 'a threat.'

depth.background: North Korea has for years used missile tests to protest joint military exercises between the **United States and South Korea**, which it portrays as invasion rehearsals even though both allies describe the drills as defensive. North Korea has continued developing its ballistic missile programs — banned under **United Nations Security Council resolutions** — despite years of international sanctions, while deepening military ties with Russia, including reportedly supplying troops and weapons for the war in Ukraine. Leader **Kim Jong Un** has repeatedly said the North will keep expanding its nuclear and missile forces rather than negotiate them away.

stories.title: Severe Tropical Storm Chan-hom makes Japan's first-ever recorded typhoon landfall in Ibaraki, disrupting Tokyo
stories.what_happened: Severe Tropical Storm Chan-hom, designated **Typhoon No. 15** by Japan, made landfall in **Ibaraki Prefecture** near Tokyo at around **8:00 p.m. local time** on Tuesday, August 11. The Japan Meteorological Agency confirmed this is the **first typhoon landfall on record in Ibaraki since 1951**. The storm had a central pressure of **980 hectopascals**, sustained winds of **25 meters per second**, and gusts up to **35 meters per second**. Authorities warned of violent winds, high waves, and heavy rain across the Kanto and Tohoku regions, with intense rain expected to continue into August 12. The storm disrupted the Obon holiday travel rush: **ANA cancelled 58 flights** out of Haneda and Narita, **JAL cancelled four**, and JR East suspended parts of its Joban rail line.
key_points: Chan-hom, Japan's **Typhoon No. 15**, made landfall in **Ibaraki Prefecture** near Tokyo on Tuesday night.
It's the **first typhoon landfall recorded in Ibaraki** since Japan began keeping records in **1951**.
The storm carried a central pressure of **980 hectopascals** and gusts up to **35 meters per second**.
**ANA cancelled 58 flights** and JAL cancelled four, disrupting the Obon holiday travel rush.
Japan's weather agency warned of violent winds, high waves, and heavy rain through **August 12**.

depth.background: Japan sits in one of the world's most typhoon-prone regions, and its meteorological agency has tracked storm landfalls in detail since 1951 — one of the most complete disaster records anywhere. The Kanto region, which includes Tokyo and Ibaraki, usually sees typhoons make landfall further south or pass offshore, so a direct hit on Ibaraki itself is statistically unusual. The storm arrived during Japan's mid-August **Obon** holiday, one of the country's busiest travel periods, when millions return to hometowns to honor ancestors.

stories.title: Germany's top general says Russia is hitting NATO with hybrid attacks 'every day' as DNA evidence emerges in a Leipzig airport drone attack
stories.what_happened: On the night of **August 4-5**, an explosive-laden drone was found on the tarmac at Leipzig/Halle Airport next to a Ukrainian An-124 cargo plane, after CCTV appeared to show it deliberately flying into the aircraft's wing; a bomb-disposal team made the unexploded device safe and no one was hurt. Five days later, German investigators recovered **DNA traces** from the drone that reportedly point toward **Lithuania**, and may connect to a **2024 arson attack** on a DHL logistics hub at the same airport — though officials caution the link isn't confirmed. A hidden antenna, believed to have relayed the drone's control signal, was found in a nearby tree. Against that backdrop, Bundeswehr chief Gen. Carsten Breuer told the Wall Street Journal that Russia is running hybrid attacks against NATO's eastern flank "every day," using drones to map weaknesses in European air defenses while also working to destabilize governments through non-military means.
key_points: Bundeswehr chief **Gen. Carsten Breuer** told the Wall Street Journal Russia is testing NATO's eastern flank with hybrid attacks **"every day"**, refining tactics for a future conflict.
Investigators say **DNA recovered from an explosive drone** that struck a Ukrainian cargo plane's wing at Leipzig Airport on **August 5** traces toward a network possibly linked to Russia's GRU.
The drone, carrying an unexploded charge, was found next to an **Antonov An-124** — a giant cargo plane used to move military and Ukraine-bound supplies.
A hidden **antenna** was found nearby, believed to have boosted the drone's control signal; a parallel Lithuanian case alleges a GRU-linked sabotage network.
Breuer says Russia is **already shifting its economy and military** toward a possible wider conflict with the West, even while still fighting in Ukraine.

depth.background: Western officials have described a rising pattern of Russian "hybrid warfare" against NATO countries over the past two years — drone incursions, arson, GPS jamming and sabotage — short of open war but designed to probe defenses and sow instability. The Leipzig incident on **August 5, 2026** was the most serious single event in that pattern so far because it targeted a strategic cargo plane tied to Ukraine's war effort, on German soil. It follows earlier US intelligence assessments, reported by the Wall Street Journal, that Russia could attempt a "limited attack" testing NATO's mutual-defense commitment (**Article 5**) as early as this autumn.

stories.title: India names Shubman Gill to captain the Sri Lanka Tests, with Bumrah and Jadeja's returns still hanging on fitness
stories.what_happened: BCCI's selection committee announced the squad on **Tuesday**, confirming **Shubman Gill** as Test captain and **KL Rahul** in the leadership group as vice-captain. Ravindra Jadeja returns to the squad after his rest period, and uncapped domestic performer **Auqib Nabi** earns his first India call-up on the back of 104 wickets across his last two Ranji Trophy seasons. Jasprit Bumrah's status remains genuinely unsettled: some reports say he has been named in the squad but will only play once he clears a fitness test with the BCCI's Centre of Excellence, while other reports say he has already been ruled out and replaced by Nabi. India also has a four-day practice match in Colombo before the series to help assess player fitness.
key_points: BCCI named its **15-man Test squad** for the two-match Sri Lanka series, starting **August 15** in Galle
**Shubman Gill** continues as captain, with **KL Rahul** as vice-captain
**Ravindra Jadeja** returns after being rested for the Afghanistan series in June
**Jasprit Bumrah**'s spot is contested — reports conflict on whether he's fully cleared or still assessing his knee
**Auqib Nabi**, a 26-year-old pacer from Jammu and Kashmir, gets a maiden call-up after **104 wickets** in two Ranji seasons

depth.background: India's Test side has been managing a wave of injuries through the middle of 2026, with fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah's fitness in particular being carefully managed by the BCCI's medical team since a knee issue first flared up around the T20 World Cup. The two-Test series against Sri Lanka — the first Test in Galle from August 15-19, the second in Colombo from August 23-27 — comes as India also manages the workload of veterans like Ravindra Jadeja, who sat out the Afghanistan series in June.

stories.title: India warns China that the Arunachal Pradesh border 'will define' ties, after unverified reports of troop activity
stories.what_happened: Unverified reports from local residents claimed Chinese troops had entered areas near Pukar La and Ollo, in the Upper Subansiri region of Arunachal Pradesh. India's Ministry of External Affairs responded on August 11 by reasserting that Arunachal Pradesh is 'an integral part of India' and warning that the state of the border 'will define' the broader bilateral relationship — without directly confirming or denying the specific troop-movement claims. The statement came five days after the two countries held their 36th round of Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC) talks in New Delhi on August 6. Notably, Arunachal Pradesh's Chief Minister Pema Khandu publicly downplayed the reports even as the central government's language stayed firm, and the Indian Army itself has not confirmed the claims.
key_points: Local residents reported **Chinese troops** entering areas near **Pukar La and Ollo** in Arunachal Pradesh's Upper Subansiri region — but this is **not yet confirmed** by the Indian Army.
India's Ministry of External Affairs said on **August 11** that the state of the border 'will define' the wider India-China relationship.
Arunachal Pradesh's own Chief Minister, **Pema Khandu**, publicly downplayed the reports — a rare public gap between state and central government messaging.
It follows the **36th round** of India-China border talks (the WMCC) held in New Delhi on **August 6**.

depth.background: India and China share a long, disputed border known as the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)**, including in Arunachal Pradesh, which China claims in its entirety as 'South Tibet' while India administers it as a full state. Relations have been cautiously stabilizing since a deadly 2020 clash in Galwan Valley, including a resumption of high-level border talks — but any reported troop movement near the LAC has historically been enough to reignite tension quickly, given how sensitive and heavily militarized the frontier is on both sides.

stories.title: US Navy fires Hellfire missiles to disable an Iran-bound cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman
stories.what_happened: On August 11, 2026, a US Navy MH-60 helicopter fired **two AGM-114 Hellfire missiles** into the stern and engine room of the Vela Nova, a Panama-flagged commercial cargo ship, after it allegedly ignored repeated radio and visual warnings to change course toward an Iranian port. The missiles knocked out its steering and propulsion, leaving it unable to maneuver and sparking a fire that the crew put out; CENTCOM confirmed no injuries. US Central Command said the blockade "remains fully enforced," reporting a cumulative total of **55 vessels turned away**, **3 disabled by force**, and **2 boarded** since April. This is the **12th ship** the US has struck overall, and the third since the blockade was reimposed in mid-July after an earlier truce fell apart.
key_points: A US Navy helicopter fired **two Hellfire missiles** into the engine and steering compartment of the Panama-flagged cargo ship **Vela Nova** on August 11, disabling it in the Gulf of Oman.
CENTCOM says the ship ignored repeated warnings to turn back from an Iranian port, breaching the US naval blockade in force since **April 2026**.
It's the **12th vessel** the US has struck since the blockade began, and the **3rd since it was reimposed on July 14** after a ceasefire collapsed.
No crew were hurt; a fire that broke out after the strike was extinguished, and CENTCOM says **55 ships** have now been turned away and **2 boarded**.
The strike lands in the middle of a **five-month standoff** over the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most important oil shipping routes.

depth.background: The US imposed a naval blockade on ships heading to Iranian ports in **April 2026**, part of an escalating pressure campaign against Tehran that has run alongside direct strikes and sanctions threats. A ceasefire period broke down, and Washington reimposed the blockade on **July 14, 2026**. Enforcement has moved from simply turning ships away to physically disabling vessels that don't comply — this is the third such disabling strike since the blockade resumed. The broader standoff centers on the **Strait of Hormuz**, the narrow waterway through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes.

stories.title: LEAP India's ₹2,480-crore IPO closes 2.84x subscribed, on track to list August 14
stories.what_happened: LEAP India's ₹2,480-crore initial public offering closed for bidding on Tuesday, its final day, having been subscribed **2.84 times** overall. The **qualified institutional buyer (QIB)** portion — typically large funds and banks — was subscribed 4.62 times, the non-institutional (high-net-worth individual) portion 4.74 times, while the retail investor quota was just barely covered at 1.01 times. In total, bids came in for **32.68 crore shares** against roughly 11.5 crore shares on offer. The company will finalize share allotments on August 12, with trading set to begin on the NSE and BSE on **August 14**.
key_points: LEAP India's **₹2,480-crore IPO** closed on its final day, subscribed **2.84 times overall**.
Qualified institutional buyers bid **4.62x** their quota and non-institutional investors **4.74x**, while retail just crossed 1x.
Bids came in for **32.68 crore shares** against 11.5 crore on offer.
Allotment is due **August 12**, with shares set to debut on the **NSE and BSE on August 14**.
It's one of **five IPOs** open this week, part of a busy August for India's primary market.

depth.background: LEAP India is a pallet-pooling and industrial-rental company — it supplies and manages reusable pallets and crates that manufacturers and retailers use to move goods through supply chains, a niche but growing logistics-infrastructure business in India. Indian IPO activity has been especially heavy this week, with LEAP India, Technocraft Ventures, Molbio Diagnostics, Dhoot Transmission, and Milky Mist Dairy all raising money from investors simultaneously — a sign of strong risk appetite in India's primary market even as broader indices have been choppy on oil-price worries.

stories.title: Government summons Air India's CEO over mid-air drop that injured 20+, as the pilot fails a second drug test
stories.what_happened: On August 4, Air India flight AI2379, an Airbus A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi carrying 137 passengers (including 3 infants) and 8 crew, suffered a sudden altitude drop of roughly 300 feet mid-flight, injuring an estimated **20 to 24 people** onboard. On August 11, the Ministry of Civil Aviation and the DGCA summoned Air India's outgoing CEO **Campbell Wilson** to explain the airline's response, with officials citing the 'fragile' state of public confidence in the wake of the AI171 crash last year. Separately, the pilot-in-command's second post-flight drug test came back as a **confirmatory positive** for marijuana, adding a conduct dimension to what began as a technical incident. India's Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has classified the event as 'serious', a category that brought in France's BEA (Bureau d'Enquêtes et d'Analyses) and Airbus itself to assist the probe.
key_points: The DGCA summoned outgoing CEO **Campbell Wilson** after flight AI2379 from Phuket suffered a sudden **300-foot** altitude drop on **August 4**, injuring around **20-24** people.
The pilot-in-command's second post-flight test came back **positive for marijuana**, turning a technical scare into a conduct scandal too.
Investigators classified the incident as **'serious'**, pulling in France's air-accident bureau (BEA) and Airbus for support.
It comes just over a year after the **AI171** crash, which officials say has left public confidence in Air India 'fragile'.

depth.background: Air India has been under Tata Group ownership since 2022, in the middle of a multi-year turnaround meant to modernize a once state-run airline with an aging safety reputation. That turnaround was already under intense scrutiny after the **AI171** crash last year, one of India's deadliest aviation disasters in decades. The **DGCA** (Directorate General of Civil Aviation) is India's aviation safety regulator, with the power to summon airline executives and ground crew over safety lapses.

stories.title: Former Australia star Moises Henriques to captain Portugal in T20 World Cup qualifiers
stories.what_happened: Henriques was named captain of Portugal's 14-player squad for the ICC T20 World Cup Europe Sub-Regional Qualifier C, being held in Finland from August 14 to 20, 2026. Portugal are grouped alongside Israel, Germany, Greece and the Czech Republic; the group winner advances toward a European regional final alongside Scotland, Jersey and Denmark, with the top finishers from that stage progressing toward the global qualifying pathway for the 2028 T20 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand. It marks Portugal's push to reach a T20 World Cup for the first time in the country's history. The squad also includes players such as Craig Cachopa, Edward Fleming and wicketkeeper Dhavalkumar Norotam.
key_points: **Moises Henriques**, 39, who retired from Australian domestic cricket last month, will captain **Portugal's** 14-player squad.
The ICC T20 World Cup **Europe Sub-Regional Qualifier C** runs in Finland from **August 14-20**.
Portugal are grouped with **Israel, Germany, Greece and the Czech Republic**; the group winner advances toward a European regional final.
It's part of Portugal's bid to reach a **T20 World Cup for the first time ever**.

depth.background: Cricket's global qualifying system lets 'associate' nations — countries without full Test-playing status — work their way toward major ICC tournaments through regional qualifiers. Henriques, born in Madeira, Portugal, played for Australia internationally and had a long IPL career including with Sunrisers Hyderabad; his Portuguese heritage makes him eligible to represent Portugal, joining a broader trend of established professionals turning out for smaller cricketing nations.

stories.title: Ferrari poaches two chassis engineers from Mercedes and Aston Martin to build its 2027 car
stories.what_happened: Ferrari has recruited two engineers from rival teams to reinforce its chassis department. Luciano Nicomede, who had spent over four years at Mercedes' Brackley factory as a composite design engineer, announced the move himself on LinkedIn. Separately, Carlos Sánchez Martínez, a chassis stress-engineering specialist who had been at Aston Martin since its Racing Point days in 2019, started at Ferrari's Maranello base in July 2026. Both now sit under chassis chief Fabio Montecchi, who reports to technical director Loïc Serra, and are reportedly already shaping the characteristics of Ferrari's 2027 monocoque — the carbon-fibre structural tub at the heart of the car.
key_points: **Luciano Nicomede**, a composite design engineer, left Mercedes after **four years** to join Ferrari's chassis team.
**Carlos Sánchez Martínez**, a stress-engineering specialist, moved over from **Aston Martin**, where he'd been since the team was Racing Point back in 2019.
Both now report to chassis chief **Fabio Montecchi** under technical director **Loïc Serra**, and are already working on Ferrari's **2027 monocoque**.
It signals Ferrari stacking specialist talent ahead of F1's next major rules reset in **2027**.

depth.background: In Formula 1, a team's chassis department — the engineers who design the car's structural 'tub' — is one of the most specialized and closely-guarded parts of the operation, and hiring away a rival's specialists is a common early signal of how seriously a team is preparing for a coming regulation change. F1 is heading into a major new technical ruleset in 2027, meaning every top team is now quietly building its next-generation car well ahead of the season it will actually race.

stories.title: Milky Mist's ₹1,553-crore IPO opens today, the largest ever by an Indian dairy company
stories.what_happened: Milky Mist Dairy Food's IPO opened for subscription today, August 11, giving investors a three-day window to bid for shares before the issue closes on **August 13**. The company has fixed a price band of **₹133 to ₹140** per share, with a lot size of 107 shares meaning a retail investor needs roughly **₹14,980** at the top end to apply for a single lot. The **₹1,553-crore** offering combines a fresh issue of 10.20 crore shares worth up to ₹1,428 crore — money that goes to the company itself — with an offer for sale of 89.28 lakh shares worth up to ₹125 crore, where existing shareholders sell down their stake. The tentative allotment date is August 14, with refunds and share credits by August 17, and listing on the NSE targeted for **August 18**.
key_points: Milky Mist Dairy Food's **₹1,553-crore IPO** opened for subscription today, closing **August 13**.
The price band is set at **₹133-₹140 per share**, with a lot size of **107 shares**.
A retail investor needs about **₹14,980** to bid for one lot at the top of the price band.
It combines a **₹1,428-crore fresh issue** with a **₹125-crore offer for sale**.
Shares are expected to list on the **NSE on August 18**.

depth.background: An **IPO (Initial Public Offering)** is when a private company sells shares to the public for the first time, raising money while letting existing owners and early investors cash out part of their stake. Milky Mist is a packaged dairy products company, and this listing is being marketed as the **largest IPO ever by an Indian dairy company**, arriving in the middle of an unusually busy week for India's primary market, which is seeing nine IPOs collectively target nearly ₹7,700 crore.

stories.title: Romania destroys two Russian-made drones found drifting near its biggest Black Sea gas project
stories.what_happened: Romanian army divers carried out a controlled detonation of **two Gerbera-type drones** found floating, not flying, in the Black Sea on August 11, Defence Minister Radu Miruță said. They were spotted by a vessel working in the area about **90 nautical miles from Constanța**, near the Neptun Deep gas project. Gerbera drones are a low-cost Russian decoy/strike drone based on Iran's Shahed design, often used alongside real attack drones to overwhelm air defenses. The operation caused no injuries or damage. Ukraine said the drones were not its own, effectively pointing to Russia as the source, though Romanian officials stopped short of formally attributing them.
key_points: Romanian navy divers destroyed **two Gerbera-type drones** found adrift in the Black Sea on August 11.
The drones were spotted roughly **90 nautical miles** off the port of Constanța, near the **Neptun Deep** gas field.
Gerbera drones are a **cheap, Russian-made decoy/attack drone**, modeled on Iran's Shahed design.
Ukraine confirmed the drones were **not its own** — leaving Russia as the likely source, though Romania hasn't formally assigned blame.
**Neptun Deep** is due to come online in 2027 and would make Romania the **EU's largest gas producer**.

depth.background: Romania is a **NATO** member and sits on the Black Sea directly across from Ukraine's Odesa region, where Russian and Ukrainian drone debris has washed up repeatedly since the war began. **Neptun Deep**, jointly owned by Austria's OMV Petrom and Romania's state gas firm Romgaz, is the country's biggest energy investment in decades — a deep-water gas field expected to sharply cut Romania's, and the region's, reliance on imported gas once it starts producing in 2027. Stray war debris drifting into NATO waters has become a recurring flashpoint, occasionally triggering fighter-jet scrambles.

stories.title: Isack Hadjar opens up on the 'culture shock' of his mid-season promotion to partner Verstappen at Red Bull
stories.what_happened: In new comments, Hadjar admitted he suffered a 'culture shock' moving from Racing Bulls, which he described as a more family-like, Italian-flavoured operation, to Red Bull's British-run senior team, despite both falling under the same parent energy-drink company. He said his years in Red Bull's junior program — including driving Verstappen's own car during a practice session at the 2024 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix — made the transition considerably less jarring than a standard move between rival constructors would have been. Hadjar also noted his working relationship with race engineer Richard 'Woody' Wood dates back three years, to those same early junior outings.
key_points: **Isack Hadjar** described switching from Racing Bulls' more 'family, Italian' environment to Red Bull's British operation as a genuine **culture shock**.
He was promoted to partner **Max Verstappen** at Red Bull after a strong rookie season in 2025.

Hadjar says his history in Red Bull's junior program — including driving Verstappen's car during practice at the **2024 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix** — made the move less jarring than a typical switch between rival teams.
His working relationship with race engineer **'Woody' (Richard Wood)** actually began three years ago during those early outings.

depth.background: Red Bull operates a junior driver 'feeder' system, historically running its sister team (now called Racing Bulls) as a proving ground before promoting drivers to the main Red Bull squad. Hadjar's promotion this season adds fresh stakes given the already-reported activation of Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause, which makes the stability of his new teammate more significant to the team's future.

stories.title: Amnesty International warns Afghanistan's cricket series in Ireland risks becoming 'Taliban propaganda'
stories.what_happened: With Ireland hosting Afghanistan for a five-match men's ODI series (two games at Bready, three at Belfast's Stormont, with Stormont fixtures on August 10, 12 and 15), Cricket Ireland has arranged security plans with the Police Service of Northern Ireland in anticipation of demonstrations. Amnesty International spokesperson Felix Jakens told BBC Sport that 'the Taliban will look to harness this series for propaganda purposes,' comparing the dynamic to other regimes using sport to 'launder their image.' Jakens called on Cricket Ireland and the ICC to keep the plight of Afghan women in focus throughout the series and to fully respect the right to peaceful protest around the matches.
key_points: Cricket Ireland has security plans in place with police as it hosts Afghanistan for a **five-match ODI series**, with fixtures at Bready and Belfast's Stormont.
Amnesty International's **Felix Jakens** said the Taliban 'will look to harness this series for propaganda purposes', comparing it to other regimes using sport to launder their image.
The controversy centers on the Taliban's near-total ban on **women's sport, education and public life** since taking power in 2021.
Amnesty is calling on Cricket Ireland and the **ICC** to keep Afghan women's exclusion in focus while still honouring the right to peaceful protest.

depth.background: Afghanistan's men's cricket team continues to compete internationally even though the Taliban government has banned women and girls from playing sport, attending school past a certain age, and taking part in most public life since retaking power in 2021. This tension has repeatedly put other cricket boards — including Australia and England — under pressure over whether continuing to play Afghanistan implicitly legitimizes the Taliban, or whether keeping the team engaged is the better way to keep pressure on the regime.

stories.title: Alpine bets its 'critical' Zandvoort upgrade on saving its shot at 5th place
stories.what_happened: Alpine driver Pierre Gasly said the team's planned upgrade package for the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort — including **'some pretty big new aero parts'** — is critical to keeping Alpine's hopes of finishing 5th in the constructors' championship alive this season. The comments came as Alpine, along with rivals like McLaren and Aston Martin, prepares to introduce significant new parts once the F1 summer break ends and the season resumes at Zandvoort on **August 21-23**. Gasly's remarks underline how much competitive pressure is riding on a single upgrade package landing correctly.
key_points: Alpine driver **Pierre Gasly** says a **big aero upgrade** due at the Dutch Grand Prix is **'critical'** for the team's 2026 hopes.
Alpine is fighting to hold onto **5th place** in the constructors' championship.
The upgrade lands at **Zandvoort (August 21-23)**, right after F1's summer break.
It follows a pattern this season of teams saving their **biggest updates** for the post-break run of races.
Rivals **McLaren** and **Aston Martin** are also pushing new parts around the same window, raising the stakes for Alpine.

depth.background: Formula 1 teams get a fixed budget each season under the **cost cap**, so most save their biggest aerodynamic upgrades for a few key races rather than spreading small tweaks all year. The August summer shutdown is a natural moment for that: teams use the forced downtime to finish parts in the factory, then bring them out together at the next race. Alpine has struggled in the midfield this year and is locked in a tight fight for 5th in the constructors' standings, a position worth significant prize money.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones set Russian oil refineries and a warehouse ablaze up to 6,500km from the front line
stories.what_happened: Overnight into August 11, Ukrainian drones struck a Wildberries logistics hub in Russia's Voronezh region, killing a **49-year-old man** hit by falling drone debris and setting fire to roughly 36,000 square metres of warehouse space. Ukraine's military separately confirmed strikes on the **Orsknefteorgsintez oil refinery** in Orenburg region, hitting a primary refining unit there, some 1,500 km from the Ukrainian border. Further east, a fire broke out at a **Rosneft refinery in Komsomolsk-on-Amur**, in Russia's Far East — over 6,500 km from Ukraine — though the exact cause and any Ukrainian link there remains unconfirmed. The strikes came the same week Russia hit Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region with North Korean-made ballistic missiles.
key_points: Ukrainian drones hit a Rosneft refinery in **Komsomolsk-on-Amur**, in Russia's Far East — roughly **6,500 km** from Ukraine.
A strike on a **Wildberries** logistics hub in Voronezh killed **one person** and tore through **36,000 square metres** of warehouse space.
Ukraine's military also confirmed hitting the **Orsknefteorgsintez refinery** in Orenburg region, about **1,500 km** from the border.
It's the latest round in Ukraine's campaign to squeeze Russia's fuel supply and its biggest e-commerce logistics network.

depth.background: Since 2025, Ukraine has run a sustained long-range drone campaign against Russian oil refineries — the plants that turn crude oil into usable fuel — aiming to choke off Russia's ability to fuel its military and economy, and it has triggered real domestic fuel shortages in Russia before. Wildberries, the target hit in Voronezh, is **Russia's largest online retailer** (similar in scale to Amazon in the US), and its warehouses have increasingly become targets as Ukraine broadens strikes to logistics infrastructure, not just energy sites.

stories.title: Sensex and Nifty slide as oil prices jump on fading hopes for a Strait of Hormuz deal
stories.what_happened: India's benchmark indices opened weak on Tuesday and extended losses through the morning: by around 11am IST, the **Nifty50 was down 112.9 points (0.46%)** at 24,470.90, and the **Sensex had fallen 362.57 points (0.46%)** to 78,177.87. The trigger is oil — **Brent crude jumped roughly 5% to settle near $87.72 a barrel** as hopes dimmed that the US and Iran will strike a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump told Axios the US is only **'semi-negotiating'** with Iran, undercutting his own earlier claims that talks were serious, while Iran has rejected direct talks and is demanding an end to the US naval blockade, sanctions relief, and compensation for war damage before it reopens shipping. Top losers on the Nifty50 included **InterGlobe Aviation, Bajaj Finance and Shriram Finance** — aviation and financing names especially sensitive to fuel and funding costs.
key_points: Nifty50 down **112.9 points (0.46%)** to 24,470.90, Sensex down **362.57 points** by mid-morning
Trigger: Brent crude jumped roughly **5% to $87.72/barrel** on fading Hormuz-deal hopes
Trump told Axios the US is only **'semi-negotiating'** with Iran, undercutting earlier talk of real progress
Top losers included **InterGlobe Aviation, Bajaj Finance, Shriram Finance** — fuel- and funding-cost sensitive names
Comes right after the **RBI defended the rupee** near 95.4/dollar over the weekend

depth.background: India imports over **80% of the crude oil** it consumes, so a sustained oil-price jump hits the economy on multiple fronts: it widens the trade deficit, pressures the rupee, and pushes up domestic fuel and transport costs that can feed into inflation. The **Strait of Hormuz** — the narrow shipping lane roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes through — has been a flashpoint for months amid the wider US-Israel-Iran standoff. The RBI had already stepped in over the weekend to defend the rupee as it neared the psychologically important 95.4-to-the-dollar level.

thread.previously: We reported the RBI stepping in to defend the rupee as rising oil prices threatened to push it past 95.4 to the dollar, while the Sensex opened flat around 24,500 as strong global cues offset a quiet start to the week.
thread.changed: That pressure has turned into an outright selloff: Brent crude jumped roughly 5% as hopes for a US-Iran deal on reopening the Strait of Hormuz faded, and both the Sensex and Nifty fell over 0.4% by mid-morning Tuesday.

stories.title: Hong Kong scientists engineer a stainless steel that could cut green hydrogen costs 40-fold by replacing titanium
stories.what_happened: A team at the **University of Hong Kong**, led by Professor Mingxin Huang, announced a new type of stainless steel — dubbed **SS-H2** — that resists severe corrosion in salty, chloride-rich conditions up to a potential of **1700 mV**, a level that matches titanium's performance. The trick is a 'sequential dual-passivation' process: alongside the standard protective chromium-oxide layer that normal stainless steel forms, a second **manganese-based layer** forms on top of it at around 720 mV, adding an extra shield against corrosion. Researchers say the manganese effect is **counter-intuitive** and contradicts existing corrosion science, and the team initially didn't believe their own results. They say the new steel could replace titanium components in electrolyzers, cutting structural material costs by roughly **40 times** and making it viable to produce hydrogen directly from **seawater** rather than purified fresh water.
key_points: New 'SS-H2' steel resists corrosion up to **1700 mV**, rivaling titanium at a fraction of the cost
Could cut structural material costs for hydrogen production by roughly **40 times**
Uses a counter-intuitive **manganese-based** second protective layer scientists say 'cannot be explained' by current corrosion science
Developed by **Professor Mingxin Huang's** team at the University of Hong Kong
Could make **seawater-based** green hydrogen production far more economical

depth.background: **Green hydrogen** — hydrogen made by splitting water using renewable electricity instead of fossil fuels — is seen as a key tool for decarbonizing heavy industry and shipping, but it's expensive partly because the electrolyzers that split water need corrosion-resistant metal parts, and the gold standard for that job is **titanium**, which is costly to mine and machine. Researchers have spent years hunting for a cheaper substitute that can survive the harsh, salty, oxidizing conditions inside an electrolyzer without corroding. The prevailing scientific view had long held that manganese actually **weakens** stainless steel's corrosion resistance, which made this particular route look like a dead end.

stories.title: Trump signals a pivot to economic pressure on Iran as the Strait of Hormuz standoff grinds past five months
stories.what_happened: President Trump told Axios he is **'low keying it'** and only 'semi-negotiating' with Iran, saying the US will let economic pressure — not further military strikes — do the work of forcing Tehran back to the table. He pointed to Iran's **'huge inflation'** and the fact that, in his telling, Iran can no longer pay its own troops, as evidence the strategy is succeeding. US Central Command said American forces had redirected **55 commercial vessels** headed toward Hormuz as of Sunday, up sharply from 35 as of August 2, and that US forces have also disabled two ships and boarded two others to enforce compliance. The Treasury separately announced its **eighth Iran sanctions package of 2026**, targeting the country's alleged shadow-banking system, which it says helps Iran evade existing sanctions. Iran, meanwhile, has issued a new list of conditions Washington must meet before it will allow normal shipping through the Strait again.
key_points: Trump told Axios he is **'low keying it'** with Iran, betting that sanctions and a naval blockade squeeze Tehran instead of further US strikes.
US Central Command says it has redirected **55 commercial vessels** as of Sunday, up from 35 on August 2, as the blockade tightens.
The Treasury issued its **eighth Iran-related sanctions round of 2026**, targeting what it calls Iran's 'shadow banking' network.
Trump cited Iran's **soaring inflation** and inability to pay its own troops as evidence the pressure campaign is working.
Iran has issued a fresh list of demands before it will reopen the Strait of Hormuz, keeping the crisis in its **sixth month**.

depth.background: The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow shipping lane between Iran and Oman through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes; Iran has kept it effectively closed for over five months amid its standoff with the US, after a missile strike hit a UAE oil tanker there and Iran's security council declared the strait would stay shut until Washington 'corrects its behavior.' Trump had weighed further military action but is now emphasizing that a US naval blockade is already straining Iran's economy. This is part of a broader 'maximum pressure' sanctions campaign the Treasury has run against Iran for most of 2026.

thread.previously: We reported Iran's security council hardening its stance and declaring the Strait would stay shut until the US 'corrects its behavior,' just as a shipping deal had appeared close.
thread.changed: Trump is now publicly shifting strategy — away from the threat of military action and toward sanctions and a naval blockade — while Iran has issued fresh demands, showing the standoff deepening rather than resolving.

stories.title: Russia strikes Ukraine with North Korean ballistic missiles for the first time, killing at least 12
stories.what_happened: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia struck the city of **Zaporizhzhia** overnight with a combination of **North Korean ballistic missiles**, Russian Zircon anti-ship missiles, and guided aerial bombs — marking the first confirmed use of North Korean-made missiles against Ukraine. Regional governor Ivan Fedorov said the Zaporizhzhia strikes killed **seven people**, all of them employees of the city's Zaporizhstal steel plant, and injured 24 others. Ukrainian officials reported **six additional deaths** from separate Russian strikes on the Dnipropetrovsk and Donetsk regions the same night, bringing the total to at least 12-13 killed. Zelensky described the attack as deliberately aimed at civilian infrastructure. Ukraine observed a day of mourning on August 12 for the victims.
key_points: Russia hit the city of **Zaporizhzhia** with **North Korean ballistic missiles**, Zircon anti-ship missiles, and guided bombs.
At least **seven people were killed** in Zaporizhzhia — all employees of the **Zaporizhstal steel plant** — with 24 injured.
**Six more people** were killed in separate Russian strikes on Dnipropetrovsk and Donetsk regions the same night.
Zelensky called it a **'vicious attack, calculated to inflict maximum damage'** on civilian infrastructure.
Ukraine held a **day of mourning on August 12** for those killed in the strikes.

depth.background: North Korea and Russia signed a mutual-defense treaty in 2024, and Pyongyang has since sent troops, artillery shells, and — as of this month — a dedicated missile unit to support Russia's war in Ukraine. Zelensky had warned just a day earlier that this was giving North Korea real combat experience it had never had, calling it a growing long-term threat. Zaporizhzhia is a frontline Ukrainian industrial city that has been repeatedly targeted by Russian strikes throughout the war.

thread.previously: On August 11, Zelensky said North Korea had begun deploying a missile unit — reportedly with 120 ballistic missiles — to western Russia, and warned this combat experience was making North Korea a bigger long-term military threat.
thread.changed: That missile unit appears to have been used within a day: Zelensky says Russia fired actual North Korean ballistic missiles at Ukraine overnight, the first confirmed use of North Korean missiles in the war, killing at least 12 people.

prev_ref.title: Zelensky warns North Korea is turning real battlefield experience against Ukraine into a bigger long-term threat

stories.title: Russia hits Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia with North Korean-made ballistic missiles, killing at least six
stories.what_happened: Russian forces launched a wave of ballistic missiles and drones at Ukraine overnight into Tuesday, August 11. In **Zaporizhzhia**, regional head Ivan Fedorov said the attack killed **six people**, injured **19**, and damaged four apartment buildings along with several non-residential buildings. President **Volodymyr Zelenskyy** said the ballistic missiles used in the strike were supplied by **North Korea**, part of a deepening military partnership between Moscow and Pyongyang. A separate missile struck near a children's hospital in Kyiv's Shevchenkivskyi district — no one was hurt there — while another strike sparked a warehouse fire that injured one person. In the central Dnipropetrovsk region, Russian drones and artillery killed three more people, including a **15-year-old boy**.
key_points: Russian forces killed at least **six people** and wounded **19** in overnight strikes on Zaporizhzhia.
President Zelenskyy says the ballistic missiles used were **supplied by North Korea**.
A separate strike hit Kyiv, sparking fires near a **children's hospital**.
**Three more people**, including a 15-year-old, died in a drone-and-artillery strike on Dnipropetrovsk.
The attack follows Kyiv's own warning that Russia is scaling up toward **200-missile mass strikes**.

depth.background: Russia has spent the summer of 2026 escalating long-range strikes on Ukrainian cities even as diplomatic efforts to end the war continue on and off. North Korea has quietly become one of Russia's most important wartime partners, supplying artillery shells and troops, and — increasingly — ballistic missile technology, in exchange for money, food, and military know-how Pyongyang badly needs. Zaporizhzhia, a frontline industrial city partly occupied by Russia since 2022, is hit regularly because of its proximity to the front line and its power infrastructure.

thread.previously: Ukraine's drone forces commander warned Russia was building toward firing roughly 200 ballistic missiles in a single combined strike — nearly triple the scale of its largest attacks so far in 2026 — and cited it as a case for hitting Russian missile factories directly.
thread.changed: That warning was followed within a day by an actual strike using North Korean-supplied ballistic missiles on Zaporizhzhia, confirming Russia is both expanding its missile supply chain and actively using the new capability.
