stories.title: VP Radhakrishnan launches 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign from the Andaman Islands, invoking Netaji's 1943 flag-hoisting
stories.what_happened: Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan travelled to **Sri Vijaya Puram** (Port Blair) in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands on Sunday to formally launch this year's **Har Ghar Tiranga Abhiyan**. He hoisted the national flag at **Flag Point**, the exact site where Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose hoisted the tricolour on **December 30, 1943**, proclaiming the islands free from British rule under the Indian National Army's brief administration. The launch coincided with **August Kranti Diwas**, marking the anniversary of the 1942 Quit India Movement against British rule. Radhakrishnan told the gathering **"Bharat is one and will always remain one,"** emphasizing unity and the sacrifices tied to the islands' history. He also attended a cultural programme and toured a **Har Ghar Tiranga exhibition** documenting the campaign's message.
key_points: Vice President **C.P. Radhakrishnan** launched this year's **Har Ghar Tiranga Abhiyan** at Sri Vijaya Puram in the **Andaman & Nicobar Islands**
He hoisted the flag at the **same spot** where **Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose** raised the tricolour on **December 30, 1943**, declaring the islands free of British rule
The launch fell on **August Kranti Diwas**, the anniversary of the 1942 **Quit India Movement**
Radhakrishnan said **"Bharat is one and will always remain one"**, framing the campaign around national unity ahead of **Independence Day**
The campaign encourages citizens nationwide to **hoist the national flag at home** through August 15

depth.background: Har Ghar Tiranga ("a flag in every home") is a now-annual government campaign, first launched in 2022 for the 75th anniversary of independence, encouraging Indians to fly the national flag at their homes in the run-up to Independence Day on August 15. The Andaman & Nicobar Islands carry particular symbolic weight for the campaign: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, leader of the **Indian National Army (INA)**, briefly took control of the islands from the British in December 1943 and hoisted the tricolour there — one of the few times the flag flew over Indian soil under Indian control before formal independence in 1947. This year's launch deliberately invoked that history.

stories.title: Sarfaraz Khan recalled to India's Test squad as Sai Sudharsan's replacement for the Sri Lanka series
stories.what_happened: Sai Sudharsan, originally picked for the Sri Lanka Tests, was ruled out after a **right toe stress reaction** picked up on India A duty, leaving India's selectors needing a like-for-like middle-order replacement just a week before the first Test. On **Sunday, August 9**, the Men's Selection Committee, headed by **Ajit Agarkar**, named **Sarfaraz Khan** as that replacement ahead of other contenders reportedly in the mix, including Shaik Rasheed and Ruturaj Gaikwad. Sarfaraz will not join the squad in Colombo immediately with the rest of the group — he links up separately before the team travels on to **Galle** for the first Test, which starts **August 15**. The call caps a comeback attempt built on sustained Ranji Trophy scoring and, by several accounts, a deliberate effort to fix the fitness weaknesses that got him dropped in the first place.
key_points: India's selection committee named **Sarfaraz Khan** as Sai Sudharsan's replacement for the two-match Sri Lanka Test series.
Sudharsan was ruled out with a **right toe stress reaction**, an injury that had reopened the fight for the No. 3 spot.
Sarfaraz, **28**, last played a Test in **November 2024** — this recall ends a **near two-year gap** from the side.
He was Mumbai's **third-highest run-scorer** in the 2025 Ranji Trophy, with **429 runs at 53.62**.
His earlier axing was widely put down to **fitness and fielding concerns**, which reports say he has since worked to address.

depth.background: Sarfaraz Khan made his India Test debut in **February 2024** and scored a century against New Zealand in Bengaluru that November, one of six Tests in which he made 371 runs. Despite a first-class average of **64.73** — among the best in the game for anyone with 50-plus innings — he was dropped soon after, with selectors citing concerns about his fitness and ground fielding rather than his batting. He has spent the time since piling up domestic runs for Mumbai and, by multiple reports, working specifically on the fitness issues that cost him his place, making this recall feel earned rather than accidental.

thread.previously: Sudharsan was ruled out of the Sri Lanka series with a toe injury, leaving India's No. 3 spot unresolved with names like Sarfaraz Khan, Shaik Rasheed and Ruturaj Gaikwad all in the frame.
thread.changed: The selectors have now settled that battle, confirming Sarfaraz Khan as Sudharsan's direct replacement in the Test squad — a recall after nearly two years out of the side.

stories.title: Mamata Banerjee's convoy pelted with mud and stones in Halisahar as TMC's post-defeat anger boils over
stories.what_happened: On Sunday, Banerjee travelled to Halisahar to meet the family of **Birju Keot**, a TMC worker who died in police custody on Saturday. As her convoy passed through the area, a crowd of local residents surrounded her vehicle, shouting 'chor' (thief) and 'dakait rani' (queen of thieves), and allegedly threw **mud, slippers and stones** at her car. Banerjee was unharmed. The protesters said they were ordinary residents without party flags, and claimed their anger stemmed from Banerjee never visiting the area during her 15 years as chief minister. Banerjee accused the BJP of orchestrating the attack, while the BJP said the reaction reflected genuine public anger rather than an organised move by its workers.
key_points: **Mamata Banerjee** was heckled and had mud, slippers and stones hurled at her car in Halisahar, North 24 Parganas
She was visiting the family of **Birju Keot**, a TMC worker who died in police custody a day earlier
Protesters chanted 'chor' (thief) and 'dakait rani' (queen of thieves) as her convoy passed
The incident comes **three months after BJP's Suvendu Adhikari ended TMC's 15-year rule** as Bengal's new CM
Banerjee blamed the **BJP** for orchestrating the protest; the BJP denied organising it

depth.background: Mamata Banerjee led the Trinamool Congress (TMC) as West Bengal's chief minister for nearly 15 years until her party's shock defeat in the **April-May 2026 assembly election**, when the BJP's Suvendu Adhikari — once her own protégé before defecting — won 208 of 294 seats and became chief minister. Banerjee, now leader of the opposition, has continued visiting grassroots TMC workers and their families as she tries to rebuild the party's standing. Halisahar, in North 24 Parganas district, has seen sporadic political violence for years as TMC and BJP compete for local control.

stories.title: Assam's Ashmita Chaliha wins her maiden BWF title, beating China's fourth seed at the Korea Masters
stories.what_happened: Ashmita Chaliha won the women's singles final at the **Korea Masters** in South Korea, defeating China's fourth seed **Han Qianxi**. Chaliha started strongly, building a 9-5 lead in the first game, but Han reeled off five straight points to snatch the opener 21-14. Chaliha regrouped, taking control at the mid-game intervals in games two and three to close out a 21-14, 21-14 win and the match in 53 minutes. It was her **maiden BWF World Tour title**, achieved on her very first appearance in a tour final. She becomes the **third Indian player in 2026** to win a Super 300 title, after Devika Sihag and Tanvi Sharma, continuing a strong year for Indian women's badminton depth beyond the established top stars.
key_points: Chaliha won the **Korea Masters Super 300** final, her **first-ever BWF World Tour title**, on her first appearance in a final.
She beat China's **fourth-seeded Han Qianxi** in a comeback win: **14-21, 21-14, 21-14** over 53 minutes.
She lost the opener after squandering a 9-5 lead, then won two straight games by closing out her interval leads.
The 26-year-old from **Assam** becomes the **third Indian woman** to win a Super 300 title in 2026, after Devika Sihag and Tanvi Sharma.
She credited her coach, **Park Tae-Sang**, for the turnaround in the final two games.

depth.background: The BWF (Badminton World Federation) World Tour is badminton's global professional circuit, with tournaments ranked by prize money and points from Super 100 up to Super 1000; a **Super 300** event sits in the middle tier but still carries real ranking points and prize money. India has built increasing depth in women's singles badminton beyond its established stars like PV Sindhu, with a new generation of players breaking through on tour in 2026. Ashmita Chaliha, from Assam, had reached quarterfinals and semifinals on tour before but had never previously won a title or even reached a final.

stories.title: India's new Test captain Shubman Gill nurses a finger injury just days before the Sri Lanka series
stories.what_happened: Shubman Gill, leading a **three-day India-A-style warm-up match** against a Sri Lanka Cricket XI ahead of the Test series, sustained an injury to his right ring finger and did not take the field on **Day 1** of the practice game, with vice-captain **KL Rahul** leading the side in his absence. By **Day 3**, Gill was seen back on the field participating in warm-up drills, seen as an encouraging sign that he could be fit for the series opener. The injury adds to India's mounting fitness concerns ahead of the tour: Bumrah is already out with a knee injury (replaced by uncapped debutant Auqib Nabi), and Sai Sudharsan is out with a toe stress fracture, while several other bowlers are also sidelined. The first Test is scheduled to begin at **Galle International Stadium on August 15**, leaving Gill only a matter of days to fully prove his fitness before India's new-captain era officially begins.
key_points: Gill, named India's new **Test captain**, sat out Day 1 of the SL warm-up game with a **right ring-finger injury**
He was seen back doing **warm-up drills ahead of Day 3**, a positive sign for his recovery
The injury comes on top of **Jasprit Bumrah** already being ruled out of the series with a knee injury
Uncapped fast bowler **Auqib Nabi** was handed a shock debut call-up to replace Bumrah
The first Test starts **August 15 in Galle**, giving Gill only days to prove his fitness

depth.background: India named **Shubman Gill** as its new Test captain for the tour of Sri Lanka, succeeding the previous leadership setup, in a squad announced in late July that also confirmed **Jasprit Bumrah** — India's premier fast bowler — would miss the series while recovering from a left knee injury sustained during the England ODI series. In Bumrah's place, uncapped **Auqib Nabi**, a Jammu and Kashmir pace bowler who took 104 wickets across the last two Ranji Trophy (India's domestic first-class) seasons, earned a surprise call-up to the senior squad. India also already ruled out batter **Sai Sudharsan** with a toe stress fracture, and has several other bowlers (Harshit Rana, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar) sidelined with injuries — making squad depth and fitness a running theme heading into the series.

stories.title: Carlos Sainz says he's hoping to take Verstappen's seat at Red Bull as his Williams frustration grows
stories.what_happened: According to a prominent F1 insider, Carlos Sainz is now hoping to be in the frame to replace Verstappen at Red Bull for 2027, motivated by growing frustration over Williams' underwhelming 2026 campaign. BBC F1 analyst Andrew Benson is doubtful this specific move happens, arguing that if Verstappen does leave Red Bull, he's more likely to end up at Mercedes or McLaren instead. Sainz is also said to have real interest in Aston Martin, if Fernando Alonso were to depart, or Alpine, if that team were to replace Franco Colapinto — giving him multiple possible paths for 2027. Separately, and adding to the pressure on Sainz's own position, Sergio Perez's management has opened talks with Williams about a deal to replace him; Perez is a free agent from Cadillac after year one of what was billed as a multi-year contract, and Williams boss James Vowles is reportedly open to the idea given Perez's substantial personal sponsorship backing.
key_points: Sainz is reportedly **'hoping'** to land Verstappen's Red Bull seat for **2027**, per a leading F1 insider.
The interest is driven by frustration at what's been a **difficult 2026 season** for Sainz at Williams.
Analyst **Andrew Benson** is sceptical, saying a departing Verstappen is more likely to land at **Mercedes or McLaren**.
Sainz also has **Aston Martin and Alpine** as possible fallback destinations for 2027.
Separately, **Sergio Perez's** management has opened talks with **Williams** about replacing Sainz there.

depth.background: Carlos Sainz joined Williams for the 2025 season after leaving Ferrari, hoping to help rebuild the historic team, but 2026 has brought fresh regulation changes that have left Williams — and Sainz — struggling for competitiveness. With Max Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause now active after a poor first half of his season, speculation has intensified across the paddock about who might replace him if he leaves.

stories.title: Mercedes' George Russell announces engagement to partner Carmen Montero Mundt
stories.what_happened: Russell announced his engagement to **Carmen Montero Mundt** on Sunday, sharing photos on social media from what appeared to be a candlelit beachside proposal, captioned simply with a ring and a heart emoji. The couple have been together **five years** since starting to date in 2020. Mundt, described as a Spanish finance professional, author and fashion influencer, has largely stayed out of the spotlight compared with some other paddock partners. The announcement drew a wave of well-wishes from the F1 paddock, including from Russell's Mercedes teammate **Kimi Antonelli** and Alpine's Pierre Gasly. The news comes a day after a difficult Belgian Grand Prix for Russell, who crashed out on the opening lap.
key_points: Russell proposed to **Carmen Montero Mundt** during a candlelit beachside dinner
The couple has been together **five years**, dating since 2020
Mundt is a **Spanish finance professional, author and fashion influencer**
Teammate **Kimi Antonelli** and rivals like Pierre Gasly sent congratulations
News breaks a day after Russell's **race-ending Belgian GP crash** on lap one

depth.background: George Russell is Mercedes' lead F1 driver, currently third in the 2026 drivers' championship behind teammate Kimi Antonelli and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton. He has dated Carmen Montero Mundt, a Spanish finance professional and social-media personality, since 2020. F1 driver personal-life news regularly draws big attention from fans given the sport's growing global following, even amid an intense on-track title fight this season.

stories.title: Scotland chase World Cup qualification points against bottom-placed UAE in Dundee
stories.what_happened: Scotland played the United Arab Emirates at Forthill in Dundee on Sunday, in the 125th match of the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2. Scotland went into the game **second in the League 2 standings with 41 points**, fresh off a nine-run victory over Canada — where **Finlay McCreath scored 112** to help set a target of 281, before Scotland restricted Canada to 272. UAE, by contrast, sit **bottom of the table with 16 points** and needed a strong result to keep their qualification prospects alive. The two sides had already met once earlier in this cycle, but that fixture was **abandoned without a ball bowled** because of rain — adding extra weight to this rematch.
key_points: Scotland (2nd in the table) face bottom-placed **UAE** in Dundee in the **ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2**
It's the 125th match of the competition — a **direct qualification pathway** toward future ODI World Cups
Scotland enter on the back of a **9-run win over Canada**, built on Finlay McCreath's 112
The two sides' earlier meeting this cycle was **abandoned without a ball bowled** due to rain
UAE, last in the table, need a big result to keep their **qualification hopes alive**

depth.background: The ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 is a multi-year one-day international competition among cricket's next tier of nations — teams below the 12 Full Members who don't get automatic ODI World Cup qualification. Results across dozens of matches in this league decide who advances toward the various World Cup qualifying events; consistent ODI cricket in League 2 also helps these teams maintain official ODI status. Scotland and UAE are two of the eight teams competing in this cycle, alongside sides like Canada, Nepal, Oman and the USA.

stories.title: Typhoon Dolphin bears down on China's coast; Shanghai evacuates 30,000 and cancels 1,384 flights
stories.what_happened: As of **August 9**, Typhoon Dolphin is approaching China's eastern coast and is forecast to make landfall between **Zhoushan city in Zhejiang** and **Fuding city in Fujian** sometime between late Sunday and early Monday. **Shanghai issued a blue typhoon alert** and has evacuated **30,300 residents** from vulnerable areas, with further relocations planned. Authorities canceled **1,384 inbound and outbound flights** — close to **60% of all flights** — at Shanghai's two airports for Sunday alone. The storm is forecast to bring wind speeds up to **70 mph**, heavy rain, and flash flooding, with impacts expected to linger across eastern China, including Shanghai and neighboring provinces, through **August 12**.
key_points: Typhoon Dolphin is set to make landfall between **Zhoushan (Zhejiang)** and **Fuding (Fujian)** late Sunday into Monday
Shanghai has evacuated **30,300 residents** from risky areas, with more relocations expected
**1,384 flights** — nearly **60% of all flights** at Shanghai's two airports — were canceled for Sunday
The storm carries wind speeds up to **70 mph** with heavy rain and flash-flood risk through **August 12**
This is the same storm that already struck Okinawa, Japan, days earlier — now threatening one of China's most populous economic hubs

depth.background: Typhoon Dolphin formed in the western Pacific in late July and was flagged by meteorologists as an unusually powerful system even before it made landfall in **Okinawa, Japan**. China's National Meteorological Center and Shanghai authorities began issuing alerts days in advance, warning that the storm's track and impact would become clearer after August 6, with Shanghai and Zhejiang province identified as the most likely landfall zone. Coastal Chinese cities regularly face summer typhoons, but the scale of Shanghai's pre-emptive evacuation signals how seriously authorities are treating Dolphin.

thread.previously: On August 8 we reported that Super Typhoon Dolphin — a storm meteorologists called unprecedented — had slammed into Okinawa, Japan and was barreling toward Shanghai.
thread.changed: Dolphin is now making landfall on China's eastern coast between Zhejiang and Fujian provinces on August 9-10. Shanghai has evacuated over 30,000 residents from at-risk areas and canceled 1,384 flights — nearly 60% of all flights at its two airports.

stories.title: India moves to hand its new rocket-launch spaceport to private companies before it's even finished
stories.what_happened: The Thoothukudi district administration confirmed the Centre has started the formal process of transferring **operation and maintenance** of the upcoming Kulasekarapattinam launch complex to private companies, even before construction is complete. The facility, built specifically to host India's Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) and future private rockets, is budgeted at roughly **₹986 crore (about $118 million)**. ISRO is targeting December 2026 for construction completion, with the site's first SSLV launch expected in 2027. Once operational, it will not be exclusive to ISRO — private Indian launch companies, including Skyroot Aerospace (which builds the Vikram series of rockets) and Agnikul Cosmos (which builds the Agnibaan), are expected to use it for their own commercial launches.
key_points: The Centre has begun handing operations of the **Kulasekarapattinam spaceport** in Tamil Nadu to private firms
It is ISRO's **second launch site** after Sriharikota, built specifically for smaller rockets like the SSLV
Private players **Skyroot Aerospace and Agnikul Cosmos** are expected to use the facility for commercial launches
The ₹986-crore facility is targeted for completion by **December 2026**, with the first launch slated for 2027
The move reflects India's post-2020 push to let private companies build and fly their own rockets

depth.background: For decades, ISRO alone owned, built and operated every Indian rocket launch from its Sriharikota spaceport. That changed after 2020 reforms opened India's space sector to private industry, creating **IN-SPACe** as a regulator to authorise private launches and **NewSpace India Limited (NSIL)** as ISRO's commercial arm. Kulasekarapattinam, on Tamil Nadu's southern coast in Thoothukudi district, was chosen as India's second spaceport because its location lets rockets launch south over open ocean — ideal for the polar and sun-synchronous orbits small satellites need — without flying over land like Sriharikota's launches must. PM Modi laid its foundation stone in February 2024, and construction on the 2,233-acre site began in March 2025.

stories.title: Germany's trade deficit with China widens to €55 billion as Chinese demand for European goods dries up
stories.what_happened: GTAI's preliminary data for the first half of 2026 shows Germany's trade deficit with China widening to about **€55 billion**, up from roughly €40 billion a year earlier. German exports to China fell by more than **12% year-on-year to just under €37 billion**, while imports from China climbed **8.9% to €91.8 billion**. As recently as 2021, China was Germany's second-biggest export market, buying €104 billion worth of German goods; today it ranks ninth. GTAI's East Asia expert, Corinne Abele, attributed the export slide to "the weak domestic economy and increasing Chinese focus on domestic value chains," adding that German firms are increasingly producing inside China itself rather than exporting to it, while China's property crisis and cash-strapped regional governments are also curbing Chinese investment and demand.
key_points: Germany's trade deficit with China widened to **€55 billion** in H1 2026, up from €40bn a year earlier
German exports to China **fell more than 12%** year-on-year to just under €37 billion
German imports from China **rose 8.9%** to €91.8 billion over the same period
China has slid from Germany's **2nd-biggest export market in 2021** to its **9th-biggest today**
Officials blame China's push for **domestic self-sufficiency**, not just a weak Chinese economy

depth.background: For two decades, China was **Germany's most important trading partner** — German carmakers, machine-tool firms and chemical giants built their growth stories around selling into a booming Chinese market. That relationship has been quietly unwinding: Chinese firms increasingly build the industrial machinery, cars and chemicals they used to import, a strategy Beijing calls **"domestic value chains."** Germany Trade & Invest (GTAI), the state agency that tracks this, has watched China's share of German exports shrink for several years running. The new H1 2026 numbers, released **August 9**, show that decline accelerating even as China remains Germany's single largest source of imports.

stories.title: Nigerian army rescues 33 civilians kidnapped by gunmen in Zamfara, forcing the attackers to flee
stories.what_happened: Troops of the Nigerian Army's 1 Brigade, operating from Forward Operating Base Tsafe, rescued **33 passengers** who had been abducted by gunmen while traveling through Magazu village in the Tsafe local government area of Zamfara state on Saturday, August 8. Acting on credible intelligence, the soldiers made contact with the kidnappers as they were moving the captives toward an undisclosed location. The troops **engaged the gunmen with effective fire**, forcing them to abandon the victims and flee into adjoining bushland. All 33 abducted persons were secured and rescued **without any casualties**.
key_points: **33 passengers** were rescued unharmed after being abducted while traveling through Zamfara state.
Troops from the **1 Brigade Forward Operating Base, Tsafe** acted on credible intelligence to intercept the kidnappers.
Soldiers engaged the gunmen with gunfire, forcing them to **abandon the captives and flee** into nearby bushland.
The rescue is part of a **years-long wave of mass kidnappings** for ransom across Nigeria's northwest.

depth.background: Northwest Nigeria has been gripped for nearly a decade by armed criminal gangs — locally called **'bandits'** — who kidnap travelers and villagers for ransom, distinct from jihadist groups like Boko Haram further northeast. Zamfara state has been one of the worst-hit, with mass abductions of bus and car passengers on rural roads a recurring event. The Nigerian military regularly runs operations against these gangs, but successful, casualty-free rescues like this one are relatively rare against a backdrop of an entrenched ransom economy.

stories.title: China claims authority to direct shipping in the Taiwan Strait during Typhoon Dolphin — Taiwan calls it 'ridiculous'
stories.what_happened: As **Super Typhoon Dolphin** barreled toward China's east coast after battering Japan's Okinawa, China's Maritime Safety Administration (Guangdong branch) announced that international shipping transiting the Taiwan Strait would have to follow its traffic-control directions for safety, with the rules taking effect **Thursday night**. Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council pushed back hard on **August 8**, calling the order 'ridiculous' and asserting that Beijing has no legal authority to restrict navigation in what Taiwan considers international waters under its own jurisdiction. Taiwanese officials said China was using the storm as a pretext to normalize the idea that it can direct traffic through the strait. Separately, Taiwan's defense ministry reported tracking **15 Chinese naval vessels and 4 military aircraft** near the island on the same day, part of the routine but closely watched pattern of Chinese military activity around Taiwan. The typhoon itself was forecast to make landfall on China's coast between Zhejiang and Fujian provinces around August 9-10, with Shanghai evacuating over 30,000 residents.
key_points: China's **Maritime Safety Administration** ordered ships transiting the Strait to follow its traffic-control directions during the typhoon
Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council called the move '**ridiculous**' and says China has no authority over international waters
Taipei accuses Beijing of using **Typhoon Dolphin as a pretext** to assert control over waters under Taiwan's jurisdiction
The order covers ships heading north through the strait's **southern entrance**, effective from Thursday night
Comes as Taiwan **tracked 15 Chinese ships and 4 military aircraft** near the island the same day

depth.background: The **Taiwan Strait** is a roughly 180-km-wide waterway separating Taiwan from mainland China, and one of the world's busiest and most contested shipping lanes — a large share of global trade and much of East Asia's energy imports pass through it. China claims the strait as its own territorial and jurisdictional waters, a position most other countries, including the US, reject; they treat it as international waters open to free navigation. China routinely uses military patrols, and now weather events, to assert de facto control without a formal declaration of sovereignty, a tactic sometimes called 'gray-zone' pressure. Tensions have been elevated for months as Taiwan's government separately moves to dissolve a pro-Beijing political party.

thread.previously: Yesterday we reported that Super Typhoon Dolphin had slammed Okinawa and was barreling toward Shanghai, forcing evacuations — the story was about the storm's physical impact.
thread.changed: Today the story has shifted to a geopolitical dispute: China used the typhoon to claim authority over shipping in the Taiwan Strait, and Taiwan is pushing back.

stories.title: F1 great Emerson Fittipaldi backs Lewis Hamilton's title push, says Ferrari's car finally suits him
stories.what_happened: Emerson Fittipaldi said this weekend he hopes to see **Lewis Hamilton** fight for the 2026 Formula 1 title, praising the improvement in Hamilton's form since he joined Ferrari. Hamilton currently sits **second** in the drivers' standings on 169 points, **50 points behind championship leader Kimi Antonelli** and **9 points ahead** of Antonelli's Mercedes teammate George Russell in third. Fittipaldi pointed to Ferrari's 2026 car as finally suiting Hamilton's driving style — a factor he says isn't getting enough attention — after Hamilton won his first race for Ferrari at the Barcelona Grand Prix earlier this season following a difficult 2025. 'I was so happy to see Lewis and Ferrari going fast,' Fittipaldi said. 'I really hope Lewis challenges for the championship.'
key_points: Two-time champion **Emerson Fittipaldi** says he hopes Hamilton 'fights for the championship'
Hamilton sits **second** in the standings, **50 points behind** leader Kimi Antonelli
He's **9 points ahead** of teammate-rival George Russell in third
Fittipaldi says Ferrari's 2026 car finally suits Hamilton's driving style, aiding his rebound
Comes after Hamilton's **first Ferrari win** at the Barcelona Grand Prix this season

depth.background: Lewis Hamilton joined Ferrari for the 2026 season after a difficult final stretch at Mercedes, and his first season in red got off to a rocky start before improving markedly in the second half. Emerson Fittipaldi, a two-time F1 world champion from the 1970s, is a respected elder statesman of the sport whose public comments carry weight, especially about the Ferrari-Hamilton pairing fans have anticipated for years.

stories.title: Israel agrees to resume Gaza ceasefire talks on August 15 after weeks of deadlock
stories.what_happened: The United States, Qatar and Egypt — the three mediators of the Gaza ceasefire — announced that Israel has agreed to resume ceasefire talks on **August 15** in Doha or Cairo. The stated goal is to '**close all remaining gaps** and commence implementation of the deal without further delay,' language that signals the deal itself isn't in dispute so much as the sequencing of who moves first. The announcement comes just days after Netanyahu publicly rejected parts of Trump's plan, insisting Israeli troops would not withdraw until Hamas fully disarms. Hamas negotiator Ghazi Hamad said the group would not implement its side of the deal unless Israel first halts attacks and begins withdrawing. Israeli strikes and incidents have continued in the interim — including gunfire on a gathering of Palestinians near Khan Younis on August 8 — even as diplomats work toward the new talks date.
key_points: Israel will restart **stalled ceasefire talks** on August 15 in Doha or Cairo
The **US, Qatar and Egypt** jointly pushed for the resumption to 'close all remaining gaps'
Comes days after Netanyahu **formally rejected** parts of Trump's 15-point Gaza plan
Hamas says it won't move until Israel **halts attacks and withdraws troops**
Over **1,230 Palestinians** have been killed since the ceasefire technically began, per Palestinian officials

depth.background: The current Gaza ceasefire, built around Trump's 20-point plan, has existed on paper since late 2025 but has never fully held in practice — Hamas's disarmament was supposed to trigger an Israeli withdrawal, but neither side trusts the other to move first. Just days ago, Netanyahu formally rejected key elements of the plan and said Israel would not withdraw until Hamas disarms, while flare-ups like Israeli strikes near Khan Younis have continued to kill and injure Palestinians despite the supposed truce. The **Board of Peace**, the international body overseeing implementation, has been shuttling between the two sides trying to find a formula both will accept. Meanwhile, Palestinian analysts say Netanyahu faces pressure to delay major concessions until after Israel's elections, expected around October 27.

thread.previously: On August 8 we reported that Israeli forces fired on Palestinians near Khan Younis and that the Board of Peace's director had reaffirmed Israel would not withdraw before Hamas's disarmament was confirmed — the ceasefire existed on paper but violence continued daily.
thread.changed: Israel has now agreed to a concrete date, August 15, to resume talks aimed at resolving that exact standoff, after mediators pushed for a breakthrough.

stories.title: George Russell warns Mercedes against complacency as its once-commanding F1 lead narrows
stories.what_happened: In an interview published this week, Russell said Mercedes must guard against **complacency** as its advantage at the front of the field narrows. Mercedes has won 8 of the 11 races run so far in 2026, but that dominance has slipped recently — **Ferrari has won twice and McLaren once** in the last five grands prix. Russell, who sits well behind teammate Antonelli in the drivers' standings after his Belgian GP crash, credited the team for how it has handled recent difficulties, including reliability concerns, but explicitly cautioned against easing off during the mid-season break.
key_points: **George Russell** says Mercedes can't afford to get **complacent** despite leading both 2026 championships
Mercedes has won **8 of 11 races** this season, but Ferrari has won twice and McLaren once in the **last five**
The warning comes as Russell's own title hopes took a hit after crashing out at the **Belgian GP**
Russell praised the team's **resilience** through recent reliability issues even while sounding the alarm
It lands during the **summer break**, before the season resumes at Zandvoort's Dutch GP on August 23

depth.background: Mercedes entered the 2026 season, under all-new technical regulations, as the team to beat, building a big early lead in both the drivers' and constructors' championships largely on the back of rookie sensation Kimi Antonelli. But form has tightened in the last month: Ferrari and McLaren have started winning races again, and Russell himself crashed out on the opening lap of the Belgian Grand Prix at Spa after what he later described on team radio as a battery-related fault, while Antonelli went on to win that race and extend his championship lead to 50 points.

stories.title: China raises Typhoon Dolphin to a red alert as landfall nears near Shanghai tonight
stories.what_happened: China's National Meteorological Centre **raised its emergency response from Level III to a red alert (Level II)** on Sunday morning as Dolphin approached the coast between Zhejiang and northern Fujian. The storm is now forecast to make landfall **Sunday evening into Monday morning**, carrying sustained winds of **162 km/h**. Authorities have relocated **nearly 99,000 people** in Fujian province alone, adding to the **30,000+** already evacuated from at-risk parts of Shanghai earlier in the week. Ports, ferries, construction work, and fishing have been suspended across Shanghai, Zhejiang and Fujian, and Shanghai has cancelled roughly **60% of its flights**. A joint red alert for flash floods now covers **23 counties and districts** in Zhejiang, where forecasters expect over **600mm of rain** — enough to trigger serious flooding. The rain band is expected to keep pushing north through Wednesday, eventually reaching Shandong, Tianjin and even Beijing.
key_points: China's weather bureau upgraded its emergency response to **red alert** (Level II) on Sunday as Dolphin closes in on the Zhejiang-Fujian coast.
Landfall is expected **Sunday evening into Monday**, with sustained winds up to **162 km/h (101 mph)**.
**Nearly 99,000 people** have been moved to safety in Fujian province alone, on top of the **30,000+** evacuated earlier in Shanghai.
A separate red alert for **flash floods** covers **23 counties and districts** in Zhejiang, where over **600mm of rain** is forecast.
Rain will keep spreading north through **Wednesday**, reaching as far as **Shandong, Tianjin and Beijing**.

depth.background: Typhoon Dolphin startled meteorologists by exploding from a tropical storm into a **Category 5-equivalent super typhoon in about 24 hours** — something China's weather bureau said it had never recorded before. It first made landfall in Japan's **Okinawa and Kagoshima** on Saturday, injuring six people and cutting power to over 50,000 buildings, before turning toward China's densely populated eastern seaboard, home to Shanghai's 25 million residents and a major chunk of the country's industrial and shipping output.

thread.previously: Dolphin exploded into a Category 5-equivalent super typhoon in 24 hours, slammed Japan's Okinawa and Kagoshima on Saturday injuring six people, and was forecast to hit China's Zhejiang-Fujian coast between Aug 9-10 after Shanghai evacuated over 30,000 people.
thread.changed: China has now upgraded to its highest (red) alert level, landfall is imminent (Sunday night into Monday), nearly 99,000 more people have been evacuated in Fujian, and a separate flash-flood red alert now covers 23 Zhejiang districts.

stories.title: Russia's overnight missile and drone strike on Odesa knocks out power to 300,000 families
stories.what_happened: Russian forces launched a combined missile-and-drone attack on Odesa region overnight into August 9, 2026, striking energy infrastructure and residential areas. Ukrainian officials said the attack **damaged residential buildings in two districts**, destroying and burning cars, and left **300,000 families without electricity**. At least 12 people were injured, with several hospitalized in moderate condition. President Volodymyr Zelensky said the outage also knocked out water pumping in parts of the city. Regional power company DTEK said repair crews were working continuously and had already reconnected roughly **90,000 of the disconnected customers** within hours, with critical infrastructure like hospitals prioritized first.
key_points: Russia hit Odesa's energy grid overnight with missiles and drones, cutting power to **300,000 families**.
At least **12-13 people were injured**, several hospitalized, after residential buildings were damaged.
The strike also **interrupted the water supply** in parts of the city by knocking out pumping stations.
About **a third of homes** had power restored within hours; repair crews worked around the clock.
It's the latest in a pattern of Russian strikes aimed at Ukraine's power grid **as winter-prep season begins**.

depth.background: Odesa is Ukraine's main Black Sea port city and has been a recurring target of Russian long-range strikes throughout the war, both for its military-shipping relevance and its civilian energy infrastructure. Russia has, over the past two winters, repeatedly targeted Ukraine's power grid in what Kyiv calls a deliberate campaign to freeze the population into submission. **DTEK**, the private company that runs much of Odesa's grid, has become practiced at emergency repairs but each strike degrades the system's redundancy further. This attack lands in the middle of an already fragile ceasefire-and-diplomacy track around the broader Russia-Ukraine war.

stories.title: Assam's flood death toll climbs to 99 as the CM tours breached embankments in Darrang
stories.what_happened: Assam's official DRIMS bulletin, released Saturday, showed the flood death toll rising to **99**, up from 98 a day earlier, with the dead comprising 58 males, 23 females and 18 children. **Cachar district** has borne the heaviest toll with 22 deaths, followed by **Sivasagar (10)**, **Karimganj (9)** and **Golaghat (7)**, with further casualties spread across Dhemaji, Nagaon, Udalguri, Sonitpur and Karbi Anglong. Chief Minister **Himanta Biswa Sarma** visited **Darrang district** to inspect embankment breaches along the **Noa and Kulsi rivers** and met displaced families sheltering in relief camps. The state government also announced it would begin a **door-to-door assessment of flood damage** starting August 9, intended to speed up permanent rehabilitation payouts for affected households.
key_points: Assam's flood death toll has risen to **99**, per the state's official DRIMS disaster bulletin
The dead include **58 males, 23 females, and 18 children** across the flood-hit state
**Cachar district** has recorded the most deaths (**22**), followed by **Sivasagar (10)**
CM **Himanta Biswa Sarma** visited **Darrang district** to inspect embankment breaches on the **Noa and Kulsi rivers**
A **door-to-door damage assessment** begins August 9 to speed up permanent rehabilitation for displaced families

depth.background: Assam has been battling a severe monsoon flood crisis through late July and August **2026**, with swollen rivers breaching embankments across multiple districts and displacing well over a lakh (100,000) people. The crisis is part of a wider pattern this monsoon season, with Kerala and Himachal Pradesh also reporting significant flood and landslide deaths in the same window. Assam's government runs the **Disaster Reporting and Information Management System (DRIMS)**, which issues the state's official daily bulletins on deaths, displacement, and relief-camp numbers.

thread.previously: On August 8 we reported Assam's flood death toll had climbed to 98, with over 1.55 lakh people affected across 13 districts and 55 relief camps running.
thread.changed: The toll has now risen to 99. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma visited Darrang district to inspect breached embankments on the Noa and Kulsi rivers, and the state has begun a door-to-door damage assessment from August 9 to speed up permanent rehabilitation.

stories.title: Masked attackers ambush a BSP leader's car at midnight in Amethi — he blames a sitting MLA's aides
stories.what_happened: According to the complaint Tiwari filed at Gauriganj police station, three unidentified men wearing masks rode up on a motorcycle near Jamo Mod late on the night of **August 8** and surrounded his car. They struck the vehicle repeatedly with sticks, rods and bricks, causing significant damage. Tiwari says the attackers fled only after he displayed his licensed pistol. He has publicly alleged that people close to sitting SP MLA Rakesh Pratap Singh were behind the ambush, though he has not named the attackers directly, and police have not confirmed any link to the legislator. Gauriganj station house officer Ravi Singh confirmed an FIR was registered against unknown persons and that an investigation is underway; no arrests had been announced as of the latest reports.
key_points: Three **masked, motorcycle-borne attackers** ambushed BSP district leader **Shashikant Tiwari's car** near Jamo Mod in Gauriganj, Amethi, around **midnight on August 8–9**.
The assailants smashed the car with **sticks, rods and bricks**; Tiwari says he escaped serious injury only after brandishing his **licensed pistol**, which scared the attackers off.
Tiwari has accused aides of **Samajwadi Party MLA Rakesh Pratap Singh** — the sitting, three-term legislator from Gauriganj — of orchestrating the attack.
Gauriganj police have registered an **FIR against unidentified assailants** and say the case is under investigation; the named MLA has not been formally charged.
Amethi has flipped between **BSP, SP, Congress and BJP** over the past decade, making it one of Uttar Pradesh's most politically contested districts.

depth.background: Amethi is one of Indian politics' most symbolically loaded districts — long a Congress-Gandhi family stronghold, lost by Rahul Gandhi to BJP's Smriti Irani in 2019, and won back for Congress by KL Sharma in 2024. Within that Lok Sabha seat sits the **Gauriganj assembly constituency**, held for three consecutive terms by Samajwadi Party's Rakesh Pratap Singh. The **Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP)**, once Uttar Pradesh's ruling party under Mayawati, has lost significant ground statewide in recent elections but still maintains a local organisational network, including district leaders like Tiwari. Political violence between rival party workers is a recurring feature of UP's local politics, especially in run-ups to civic and byelection contests.

stories.title: Russia claims two more Donetsk villages as its slow, grinding advance through eastern Ukraine continues
stories.what_happened: Russia's state-run **RIA Novosti** news agency reported on Sunday, citing the Russian Defence Ministry, that Russian forces had seized **Vasyutinske**, a few kilometers east of Kramatorsk, and **Toretsk**, southwest of the city of Druzhkivka. Ukraine's military made **no acknowledgement** that either settlement had changed hands, and Reuters said it could not independently verify the Russian claims — a routine caveat, since both sides regularly make contested territorial claims in this war. The broader picture, per Reuters' battlefield tracking, is that Russia continues to advance slowly westward through Donetsk, with **little significant change** in overall front-line positions for months despite a steady drip of small village captures like this one.
key_points: Russia's Defence Ministry says its forces captured **Vasyutinske and Toretsk**, two villages in Ukraine's Donetsk region, on **Sunday**.
Vasyutinske sits just a few kilometers east of **Kramatorsk**, one of the last major Ukrainian-held 'fortress cities' in the region.
**Ukraine has not confirmed** either village fell, and Reuters says it could not independently verify Russia's claim.
The front line has barely shifted for months even as these small captures accumulate, stretching **1,200 km** north to south.
This is how Russia is actually advancing now — **village by village**, not through any single dramatic breakthrough.

depth.background: Russia annexed Crimea in 2014 and backed separatists in Ukraine's eastern Donetsk and Luhansk regions; its full-scale invasion in February 2022 turned that low-level conflict into all-out war. For roughly the last year, the war has settled into a grinding, attritional pattern along a **1,200-km front line** — neither side has managed a major breakthrough, but Russia has kept inching forward by taking small settlements one at a time. **Kramatorsk**, near where Vasyutinske sits, is one of the last major Ukrainian strongholds in Donetsk province; its loss would open the way toward other Ukrainian defensive lines further west.

stories.title: PM Modi honours India's 39-medal Commonwealth Games contingent, led by a record boxing haul
stories.what_happened: India's contingent of 122 athletes returned from Glasgow with **39 medals** — 13 gold, 17 silver and 9 bronze — placing the country **4th overall** in the medal table. **Boxing was the standout discipline**, delivering 10 of India's medals including seven golds, the most golds any country has ever won in boxing at one Commonwealth Games. Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosted the medal-winning athletes at his residence, congratulating them individually; among those present were weightlifter and Olympic champion Mirabai Chanu and boxer Lovlina Borgohain.
key_points: India won **39 medals** — **13 gold, 17 silver, 9 bronze** — at the **2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow**, finishing **4th** in the medal table.
Just **122 athletes** competed across 8 able-bodied sports and 5 integrated para sports.
**Boxing led the medal count** with 10 medals, including a record **7 golds** — the most any nation has won in boxing at a single Commonwealth Games.
PM Modi met and honoured the medalists at his residence, including **Olympic champion Mirabai Chanu** and boxer **Lovlina Borgohain**.

depth.background: The **Commonwealth Games** is a multi-sport event held every four years among countries of the former British Empire (the 'Commonwealth'), similar in spirit to a smaller Olympics. India has historically used it as a proving ground for athletes ahead of Olympic cycles, particularly in boxing, wrestling, weightlifting and badminton. The 2026 edition was hosted in **Glasgow, Scotland**.

stories.title: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak becomes the world's second-largest on record — over 300 children dead — as WHO urges a vaccine trial
stories.what_happened: The outbreak has grown faster than almost any Ebola outbreak on record, reaching over **4,000 confirmed cases** and more than **1,500 deaths** in under three months — a scale that took nearly two years to reach in the DRC's previous major outbreak (2018–2020). Health officials say **more than 300 children** have died, a disproportionate toll given children make up about a quarter of all cases. In response, a WHO Technical Advisory Group recommended in a report issued Friday that the existing licensed vaccine, **Ervebo**, be tested in a randomized clinical trial against the Bundibugyo strain specifically, after animal studies suggested it might offer partial cross-protection, particularly against death. Separately, Moderna has begun a Phase 1 human trial of an mRNA vaccine candidate (mRNA-1469) built specifically for this strain, vaccinating its first participants in Canada. Currently, **694 patients** are hospitalized in isolation, and 53 of 140 health zones across five provinces are affected, with Ituri province alone accounting for the large majority of cases.
key_points: The outbreak has surpassed **4,000 confirmed cases** and **1,500+ deaths** since it was declared on **May 15, 2026**.
It is now the **second-largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded**, behind only the 2014–16 West Africa epidemic (28,600+ cases).
More than **300 children** have died — children make up nearly a quarter of cases but almost a third of deaths.

A WHO expert panel has recommended testing the licensed **Ervebo vaccine** in a randomized trial against this outbreak's less-common **Bundibugyo virus strain**, which the vaccine wasn't originally designed for.
**Moderna** has separately begun a Phase 1 trial of an mRNA vaccine candidate specifically targeting the Bundibugyo strain.

depth.background: Ebola is a severe, often fatal viral disease that spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids, with outbreaks historically concentrated in Central and East Africa. Most past Ebola outbreaks were caused by the 'Zaire' strain, for which the existing Ervebo vaccine was specifically developed and proven highly effective. This outbreak — declared in the DRC's Ituri province in mid-May 2026 — is caused by the rarer **Bundibugyo virus** species, for which no vaccine has ever been formally proven effective. The World Health Organization declared it a **Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC)** on May 17, its highest alert level, and the outbreak has since spread into neighboring **Uganda** and across five DRC provinces, compounded by ongoing armed conflict that has displaced nearly a million people in the region and makes contact-tracing and treatment access far harder.

stories.title: Audi F1 boss Mattia Binotto breaks his silence on Carlos Sainz rumours as 'silly season' hits overdrive
stories.what_happened: With Williams enduring a difficult start to the 2026 season, reports have intensified that **Carlos Sainz** is reconsidering the Audi move he turned down two years ago, given his existing relationship with team principal Mattia Binotto from their Ferrari days together. Binotto addressed the speculation publicly for the first time this week, suggesting Audi's current pairing of Hulkenberg and Bortoleto — both believed to be on longer-term contracts — is likely to continue into 2027, even as he acknowledged Audi is an 'obvious' landing spot people would link Sainz to. Sainz himself has reportedly asked his management team to keep him out of driver-market conversations until after the summer break, when he plans to make a decision on his 2027 future.
key_points: **Carlos Sainz** is reportedly weighing a return to **Audi** for 2027, the team he rejected two years ago to join Williams.
Audi F1 chief **Mattia Binotto** — Sainz's former boss at Ferrari — has publicly addressed the rumours for the first time.
Binotto suggested Audi's lineup of **Nico Hulkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto** will likely stay unchanged for 2027.
Sainz reportedly asked his management to hold off on driver-market talk until after the **summer break**, when he'll decide his future.
Williams' rocky start to the 2026 season is reportedly a key factor pushing Sainz to reconsider his options.

depth.background: Carlos Sainz left Ferrari at the end of 2024 and chose to join Williams for 2025 over reported interest from Audi, betting on Williams' long-term rebuild under new ownership. Audi entered F1 as a full works team in 2026 by taking over the Sauber outfit, bringing in **Mattia Binotto** — Sainz's former Ferrari team principal — to lead the project, alongside drivers Nico Hulkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto. F1's driver market reshuffles heavily during the **summer break**, the sport's mandatory shutdown period, as teams and drivers use the pause to finalize contracts for the following season without the distraction of race weekends.

stories.title: Fernando Alonso names a window — Zandvoort to Monza — for deciding whether he races on in F1 for 2027
stories.what_happened: Speaking to media, Alonso said: **'I have not taken any decision; I will wait until probably summer break, which is August, and after summer it's Zandvoort, Monza — I think around that time I will probably decide what to do next year.'** That places his decision window in the run of races following the summer break, from the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort through the Italian Grand Prix at Monza. He explicitly said Aston Martin's disappointing 2026 season — the team sits 19th in the drivers' standings — will **not** be the deciding factor; instead, he says the current regulations and whether the cars still give him the enjoyment he wants to keep racing are the bigger question. He has confirmed he intends to keep racing in some capacity in 2027 regardless, but hasn't committed to that being in Formula 1. Team principal and design chief Adrian Newey separately said he is 'pretty confident' Alonso will stay, pointing to an incoming Honda engine upgrade debuting at Zandvoort as a potential turning point for the car.
key_points: Alonso, **44**, says he'll decide his 2027 plans **between the Dutch GP (Zandvoort) and Italian GP (Monza)**, late August into September.
He's confirmed he'll **keep racing in some form** in 2027 — just not necessarily in Formula 1.
Alonso says the call hinges on **the current-generation cars and regulations**, not Aston Martin's poor 2026 form.
Aston Martin sits **19th** in the drivers' standings this season, a near-pointless year for the team.
Team boss and design chief **Adrian Newey** says he's 'pretty confident' Alonso stays for 2027.

depth.background: Fernando Alonso is a two-time F1 world champion (2005, 2006) who returned to Aston Martin as the team built around him, hiring legendary designer **Adrian Newey** to lead its technical push for the new-generation regulations that arrived in 2026. Those new rules were supposed to level the playing field, but Aston Martin has instead had a difficult first half of the season, leaving Alonso, at 44, deep in the drivers' standings and facing genuine questions about whether continuing is worth it. He has said before that his motivation is tied more to whether the cars themselves are still exciting to drive under the new rules than to whether his team is winning.

stories.title: Iran's security council declares the Strait of Hormuz stays shut until the US 'corrects its behavior,' hardening its stance just as a shipping deal neared completion
stories.what_happened: Iran's **Supreme National Security Council** said in a statement carried by state broadcaster that the Strait of Hormuz will not open until the United States **'corrects its behavior,'** according to council secretary **Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr**. The council laid out **six specific conditions**: the US must never threaten Iran again and must permanently end its war against Iran and its regional allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen and Iraq; lift its **naval blockade** and withdraw military forces from around Iran; **'completely compensate'** Iran for damage from what it calls two imposed wars; lift sanctions; and unconditionally release Iran's **frozen assets**. The statement came just a day after Iran's foreign minister **Abbas Araghchi** had called a separate, more technical Oman-brokered shipping-lane arrangement 'very close' to completion. It also follows a missile strike on a **UAE-flagged tanker linked to state oil firm ADNOC** as it transited the strait, which the UAE, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the Gulf Cooperation Council all condemned as a dangerous escalation. Analysts described Iran's new list as demands **'the US clearly cannot accept,'** widening the gap between technical progress on shipping lanes and the political conditions Tehran is now attaching to any real reopening.
key_points: **Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr**, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council and a senior **Revolutionary Guard** commander, said the strait won't reopen until the US **'corrects its behavior.'**
Iran listed **six conditions**, including a full US troop withdrawal from the region, **war reparations**, lifted sanctions, and the **unconditional release of frozen Iranian assets**.
The demands land just a day after Iran and Oman said a **technical shipping-lane deal** was 'very close' — showing the political price tag is far steeper than the logistics suggested.
Analysts say the list contains conditions the **US 'clearly cannot accept,'** raising the risk Trump reverts to the **military option**.
It follows a missile strike days earlier on a **UAE-flagged, ADNOC-linked tanker** in the strait, which Gulf states condemned as an act of piracy.

depth.background: The **Strait of Hormuz** is the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman that roughly **a fifth of the world's oil** must sail through, and it has been repeatedly targeted by missiles and drones since the 2026 Iran war escalated. For weeks, Oman has quietly brokered a technical arrangement — separate shipping lanes for inbound and outbound tankers — to keep commercial traffic moving safely, and that technical piece appeared close to done. But Iran has always maintained that a full, unrestricted reopening depends on the **US honoring a disputed June memorandum of understanding**, and Tehran has repeatedly accused Washington of violating it. **Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr**, who leads Iran's top security body and holds senior rank in the **Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC)**, is one of the country's most hawkish voices on the standoff.

thread.previously: On August 9 we reported that Iran and Oman had agreed on exact shipping-lane coordinates through the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran's foreign minister calling a full deal 'very close' — though a full reopening still hinged on the US honoring a disputed June memorandum.
thread.changed: Iran's Supreme National Security Council has now publicly hardened that position, listing six sweeping demands — from a US troop withdrawal to war reparations — as conditions for actually reopening the strait, demands analysts say the US 'clearly cannot accept.'

stories.title: A fast-moving wildfire destroys homes and forces over 20,000 people to flee in British Columbia, prompting a province-wide state of emergency
stories.what_happened: The **Bald Range wildfire**, first reported Friday evening near Summerland in British Columbia's Okanagan Valley, grew explosively overnight, expanding from about **103 to 136 square kilometres** by Sunday. Fire behaviour analysts rated it **'Rank 6'** — the highest classification a wildfire can reach — with embers carried up to **one kilometre** ahead of the main fire, sparking new spot fires faster than crews could contain them. Authorities ordered the **entire town of Summerland (around 12,000 people)** evacuated, along with roughly **8,000 more residents** in and around Peachland, pushing the total displaced past **20,000**. British Columbia Premier **David Eby** confirmed homes have been destroyed, and the small community of **Faulder**, which lay directly in the fire's path, is believed to have lost many structures, though officials have not yet released a formal damage count. The province declared a **state of emergency on Saturday**, and by Sunday evacuation orders and alerts stretched from the edge of Penticton in the south to Highway 97C in the north.
key_points: The **Bald Range wildfire** near Summerland, B.C. grew from **103 to 136 square kilometres** in a single day (Sunday).
More than **20,000 people** were ordered to evacuate, including the entire town of **Summerland (about 12,000 residents)**.
British Columbia declared a **province-wide state of emergency** as the fire showed the most extreme possible **'Rank 6' fire behaviour**.
Homes have already been lost, with the small community of **Faulder** believed largely destroyed, though no official damage tally exists yet.
Embers were observed jumping **1 kilometre ahead** of the main fire front, igniting new spot fires faster than crews could contain them.

depth.background: British Columbia has had increasingly severe wildfire seasons over the past decade, driven by hotter, drier summers that scientists link to climate change — **2023 was the province's worst fire year on record**, and 2026 is shaping up to rival it. The Okanagan Valley, where Summerland and Peachland sit along **Okanagan Lake**, is a densely populated wine-and-orchard region that has burned before, including the destructive 2023 McDougall Creek fire nearby. The Bald Range fire was first spotted Friday evening as a small blaze but exploded in size within hours as hot, dry, windy conditions pushed it toward populated areas. A **province-wide state of emergency** hands British Columbia's government sweeping powers — from commandeering equipment to restricting travel — to coordinate the response across multiple simultaneous wildfires.

stories.title: Ukraine sets Russia's Ilsky and Syzran oil refineries ablaze as Moscow strikes Kyiv's defence industry overnight
stories.what_happened: Ukraine's military said its drones struck the **Ilsky oil refinery** in Russia's Krasnodar region and the **Syzran refinery** further north overnight, starting fires at both sites. Local Russian officials said falling drone debris near Ilsky injured **five people**, and the fire there was later extinguished. Ukraine's general staff framed the strikes as targeting fuel supplies that keep the Russian armed forces running — Ilsky has a design capacity of over **6 million metric tons of oil a year**, Syzran about **8.5 million tons**. The following night, Russia struck back at a **military-industrial enterprise and a fuel-and-lubricants warehouse in the Kyiv region** using precision ground-based weapons. Ukrainian President **Volodymyr Zelensky** responded by pointing to the value of Western-supplied Patriot air-defence batteries, saying they protect people only when actually deployed rather than left in storage. Separately, Ukraine's naval drone forces said they struck **12 more vessels of Russia's 'shadow fleet'** — ships used to move sanctioned Russian oil — over the preceding week.
key_points: Ukrainian drones hit the **Ilsky** and **Syzran** refineries in Russia, sparking fires at both overnight into August 8.
Together the two plants can process roughly **14.5 million tonnes of oil a year** — a serious dent in Russia's fuel supply.
Debris from the strikes **injured five people** near Ilsky, according to the regional task force.
Hours later, Russia hit a **Kyiv defence-industry site and a fuel depot** with precision missiles overnight into August 9.
Ukraine says the refinery campaign is meant to starve Russia's **war machine of fuel**, not just make headlines.

depth.background: Since 2024, Ukraine has run a sustained drone campaign against Russian oil refineries, arguing that petroleum products — not just tanks and shells — are what keeps Russia's military moving. The **Ilsky refinery in Krasnodar** and the **Syzran refinery** on the Volga are both repeat targets: Ilsky alone has been hit multiple times in 2026. Russia, in turn, keeps striking Ukrainian cities and infrastructure, including defence plants around Kyiv, in an effort to grind down Ukraine's ability to arm itself and to punish the drone campaign. Both sides increasingly treat energy and industrial infrastructure — not just the front line — as the real battleground.

stories.title: Ferrari fined €30,000 after Hamilton's car strikes a mechanic on pit release at the Belgian GP; Hamilton avoids penalty
stories.what_happened: As Hamilton's Ferrari was released from a pit stop on **lap 20** of the Belgian Grand Prix, a mechanic stepped into the path of the moving front-right tyre and was struck, falling to the ground. F1's medical team confirmed the mechanic was **not injured**. Ferrari acknowledged the release was unsafe, attributing it to an **inappropriately late instruction to adjust the car's wing**, poor communication within the crew, and the mechanic failing to notice the release light had turned green. The stewards investigated and handed **Ferrari a €30,000 fine**, of which €10,000 is suspended for 12 months on the condition the team doesn't repeat the offence and submits a report on the safety protocols it will introduce. Crucially, the stewards ruled that **Hamilton himself was not at fault** and that the incident did not justify a sporting penalty against him — he kept his fourth-place finish, having earlier served a five-second penalty for separate contact with Mercedes' George Russell.
key_points: Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari struck a **mechanic** as it was released from a pit stop during the Belgian Grand Prix.
The mechanic **stepped into the tyre's path** and fell, but was **not injured**, F1's governing body confirmed.
Stewards fined Ferrari **€30,000**, with **€10,000 suspended for 12 months** pending no repeat incident.
Hamilton himself was **cleared of a sporting penalty** — stewards found the release error was the team's fault, not his.
Ferrari blamed a **late wing-adjustment instruction** and unclear communication for the mechanic missing the green light.

depth.background: Unsafe pit releases — where a car leaves its pit box before it's safe to do so — are treated seriously in Formula 1 because pit lanes are crowded with mechanics working at close range to fast-moving cars; incidents have caused serious injuries in the sport's history. The FIA's stewards investigate any release where a crew member is put at risk, weighing whether to penalize the driver, the team, or both depending on who was at fault. This incident happened during a chaotic Belgian Grand Prix weekend at Spa-Francorchamps that had already seen a first-lap crash for George Russell and a decisive win for Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli, who extended his championship lead.

stories.title: Shubman Gill returns to batting pain-free, clearing the last doubt before India's Sri Lanka Tests
stories.what_happened: Gill returned to batting practice in the nets on **Sunday**, showing no visible discomfort after his right ring-finger injury. He had missed India's three-day warm-up match against Sri Lanka Cricket XI as a precaution after being hit on the finger during practice the previous Thursday, with KL Rahul captaining in his absence. Assistant coach Bahutule said the decision to rest him for the warm-up game was "just a precaution more than anything else." With Gill now batting freely, India's camp has one less injury doubt heading into a series they've already approached short-handed, having also lost Bumrah and Washington Sundar to unrelated injuries. The first Test begins in **Galle on August 15**, with the second and final Test at Colombo's SSC Ground from **August 23-27**.
key_points: India captain **Shubman Gill** batted in the nets **pain-free** on Sunday, easing fitness fears before the Sri Lanka Tests.
Gill had been hit on his **right ring finger** during a practice session on **Thursday**, forcing him out of the three-day warm-up match.
**KL Rahul** led India in that warm-up game with Gill sidelined; Gill's return removes the doubt over his availability.
The first Test starts in **Galle on August 15**, with the second at Colombo's **SSC Ground from August 23-27**.
Team management called the injury **"just a precaution more than anything else."**

depth.background: **Shubman Gill** is India's Test captain, and his fitness heading into an away series matters both for India's batting lineup and team leadership continuity. India already went into this **Sri Lanka tour with injury concerns**, having lost key players including **Jasprit Bumrah and Washington Sundar** to injury ahead of the series. Gill was hit on his right ring finger during a practice session last Thursday, serious enough that he sat out the subsequent three-day warm-up match against a Sri Lanka Cricket XI, with vice-captain **KL Rahul** leading the side in his place.

thread.previously: We reported Gill took a fresh finger knock during the India A warm-up win over Sri Lanka XI but was provisionally cleared for the first Test.
thread.changed: Gill has now batted in the nets fully pain-free, removing the lingering doubt over his fitness heading into the August 15 Galle Test.

stories.title: India extends Enforcement Directorate chief Rahul Navin's tenure by a year, to August 2027
stories.what_happened: India's Appointments Committee of the Cabinet approved a one-year extension for Enforcement Directorate Director Rahul Navin, keeping him in the post until August 13, 2027, according to an order issued August 8. Navin, a 1993-batch Indian Revenue Service officer with more than three decades in the Income Tax Department, had been due to complete his term on August 13, 2026. He first took charge of the ED as interim chief before being made full-time director.
key_points: The government extended **Enforcement Directorate (ED) Director Rahul Navin's** tenure by **one year**, through **August 2027**.
Navin is a **1993-batch Indian Revenue Service officer** with over **30 years** in the Income Tax Department.
The order came from the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet**, days before his term was due to end on **August 13**.
The ED — India's top financial-crime and money-laundering investigator — has repeatedly seen its chiefs' tenures extended.

depth.background: The Enforcement Directorate is India's federal agency for investigating money laundering, foreign-exchange violations, and financial crime — roughly comparable to a mix of the FBI's financial-crimes unit and a currency-control regulator. In recent years it has become one of India's most politically consequential agencies, repeatedly used, opposition parties allege, to investigate rival politicians — drawing both government praise and accusations of selective targeting from critics. Navin took over as ED chief after his predecessor Sanjay Kumar Mishra's own tenure, itself controversially extended multiple times, finally ended.

stories.title: AAP accuses Delhi's BJP government of a ₹22,000 crore subsidised rice scam
stories.what_happened: AAP leader and former Delhi minister **Saurabh Bharadwaj** alleged Sunday that the BJP-led Delhi government had orchestrated a **₹22,000 crore subsidised rice scam** designed to run over three years. He claimed Delhi's food, supplies and consumer affairs department, headed by minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa, formally requested **31,000 metric tonnes of subsidised rice per week** from the FCI, ostensibly to route to a corporation based in Assam. Bharadwaj alleged that none of this rice actually reached poor households, and was instead diverted and sold to a **private company in Haryana** for profit. He said the rice was bought at around **₹23.20 per kg** and resold in the open market at **₹46 per kg**, a margin of about ₹23/kg that added up to roughly **₹143 crore a week**. There has been no immediate response from the BJP or the FCI.
key_points: AAP alleges a **₹22,000 crore** rice scam planned over three years
Claims Delhi's food ministry sought **31,000 metric tonnes of rice weekly** from the FCI
Says subsidised rice meant for the poor was allegedly **resold to a private Haryana firm** at nearly double the price
Alleges a **₹143 crore-a-week** profit margin — rice bought at ₹23.20/kg, resold at ₹46/kg
Names Delhi's food minister **Manjinder Singh Sirsa**; BJP and FCI have not yet responded

depth.background: Delhi's government runs a subsidised food-grain distribution system, buying rice cheaply from the central government's Food Corporation of India (FCI) to distribute to poorer households under India's public distribution system. AAP, which lost power in Delhi to the BJP in 2025 elections, has repeatedly accused the new BJP-led Delhi government of corruption in welfare schemes, and this allegation continues that pattern of political sparring over who is failing Delhi's poor.

stories.title: Raj Thackeray accuses Maharashtra government of hiding 'Third Mumbai' plans as land-acquisition anger builds in Raigad
stories.what_happened: Raj Thackeray publicly accused the Maharashtra government of failing to properly inform residents of Raigad district's Pen, Panvel and Uran talukas about the scope and impact of the Third Mumbai project. He said the roughly **323-square-kilometre** development across **124 villages** will primarily benefit outsiders and investors while destroying the livelihoods of local landowners and farmers whose land is being acquired under the state's new land policy. That policy returns **22.5% of developed land** to original owners once the area is built up, but Thackeray argues this doesn't adequately compensate residents for the loss of their existing, largely agricultural, livelihoods. He appealed directly to residents to **resist selling their land** and to oppose the acquisition process.
key_points: MNS chief **Raj Thackeray** accused the state government of keeping locals **"in the dark"** about the **Third Mumbai** project
Third Mumbai (the **Karnala-Sai-Chirner** new town) spans roughly **323 sq km across 124 villages** in coastal **Raigad district**
The state has finalised a land policy giving **22.5% of developed land back** to the original owners whose land is acquired
Thackeray says the project will **destroy local livelihoods** and mainly benefit **outsiders**, not residents of Pen, Panvel and Uran
He's calling on residents **not to sell their land** and to actively **oppose** the acquisition drive

depth.background: Third Mumbai is Maharashtra's plan to build a new satellite business hub southeast of Mumbai, in the coastal Raigad district, to relieve pressure on the overcrowded Mumbai Metropolitan Region and create a new economic center — sometimes pitched as the state's "next business capital." The government's land-acquisition-and-distribution policy, finalised this year, involves taking farmland and other property from local owners, developing it, and returning a portion (22.5%) to them once built up. The Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS), led by Raj Thackeray, has a long history of positioning itself as a defender of Marathi and local identity against projects it frames as benefiting outside investors and migrants over native residents.

stories.title: US Vice President JD Vance calls PM Modi to 'deepen' India-US ties as tariff and Russia-oil tensions simmer
stories.what_happened: US Vice President **JD Vance** telephoned Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** on Saturday, **August 8**, to discuss expanding the India-US 'comprehensive global strategic' relationship, according to readouts from both sides. The two leaders reaffirmed commitment to deepening cooperation across **trade, defence, emerging technologies, energy security and critical minerals**, and noted the sustained momentum of recent high-level engagement between the two countries. The call landed just a day after India's government stayed conspicuously silent following the **US Senate's passage of a sanctions bill** threatening 100% tariffs on nations, including India, that continue buying discounted Russian oil. Modi also used the call to personally congratulate Vance and his wife Usha on the recent birth of their son.
key_points: US VP **JD Vance** called PM **Narendra Modi** on **August 8** to discuss deepening India-US ties
The two leaders reaffirmed cooperation on **trade, defence, critical minerals and energy security**
The call comes as a **Russia sanctions bill** threatening **100% tariffs** on India over Russian oil purchases looms in the background
India-US ties had **soured last year** after Washington imposed punitive tariffs tied to India's Russian oil imports
Modi used the call to **congratulate Vance** on the birth of his son with wife Usha Vance

depth.background: India-US relations hit a rough patch in **2025** after Washington imposed steep punitive tariffs on Indian goods, explicitly tied to India's continued purchases of discounted Russian crude oil — a trade Delhi has defended as an energy-security necessity. Trump's repeated public claims that he personally helped de-escalate the **May 2025 India-Pakistan military clashes** also drew sharp pushback from Indian officials, who reject any suggestion of third-party mediation on Kashmir-related issues. In recent months both governments have worked to repair the relationship and move toward a trade deal, even as a new US Senate bill threatens **100% tariffs** on any country, including India, that keeps buying Russian oil.

thread.previously: On August 8 we reported that India was staying publicly silent as the US Senate's sweeping Russia-Iran sanctions bill — which threatens 100% tariffs on countries buying discounted Russian oil, including India — put trade talks and India's energy security on a collision course.
thread.changed: A day later, US Vice President JD Vance called PM Modi directly to discuss deepening the India-US relationship — a signal both sides want to keep repairing ties even as the sanctions threat hangs over trade talks.
