stories.title: India's Sri Lanka tour warm-up ends in a draw as Padikkal's maiden century sets up the Test series
stories.what_happened: The three-day tour match between **Sri Lanka Cricket XI** and **India** at the Nondescripts Cricket Club Ground in Colombo, played **August 7-9**, ended in a **draw**. India's reply to SLCXI's 363/8 declared was anchored by **Devdutt Padikkal**, who finished unbeaten on a maiden century of **142** off 164 balls, well supported by **KL Rahul (40)**, **Ravindra Jadeja (63)** and **Manav Suthar (41)**, with India closing on 357/6. The match provided India's batting order — several members of which will feature in the upcoming Test squad — valuable time in the middle heading into the series proper. India's tour continues with the **1st Test at Galle from August 15-19**, followed by the **2nd Test at Colombo (SSC) from August 23-27**.
key_points: India's three-day tour warm-up against **Sri Lanka Cricket XI** in Colombo ended in a **draw**
**Devdutt Padikkal** finished unbeaten on a maiden ton of **142**, India's standout batting performance
**KL Rahul (40)**, **Ravindra Jadeja (63)** and **Manav Suthar (41)** also made starts in India's reply of 357/6
The result gives India's batting order valuable middle time ahead of the **1st Test at Galle, August 15-19**
India's **2nd Test** against Sri Lanka follows at **Colombo (SSC), August 23-27**

depth.background: India is on a multi-format tour of **Sri Lanka** in August 2026, opening with a **three-day warm-up tour match** against a Sri Lanka Cricket XI in Colombo before the main **Test series** begins. Warm-up matches like this one are used by touring sides to get batters and bowlers match-fit and to test combinations before the higher-stakes Test fixtures. Sri Lanka Cricket XI had posted **363/8 declared** in their first innings, setting India a stiff target to match in reply.

thread.previously: On August 8 we reported Devdutt Padikkal's unbeaten 142 had dragged India level with Sri Lanka Cricket XI on Day 2 of their tour warm-up in Colombo, after India replied to SLCXI's 363/8 declared with 357/6.
thread.changed: The three-day tour match has now concluded in a draw at Colombo (NCC), giving India's batting order — including Padikkal, KL Rahul, Ravindra Jadeja and Manav Suthar, who all made starts — useful time in the middle just ahead of the first Test.

stories.title: Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson says his team is having its 'strongest' F1 season yet, as Red Bull decides his 2027 future
stories.what_happened: Speaking during F1's summer break, Lawson said Racing Bulls is enjoying **'by far'** its strongest campaign of the current regulations era, pointing to a first half of 2026 in which he has **scored points in all but three races**, while rookie teammate Arvid Lindblad is riding a **six-race points streak**. Lawson said conversations about his 2027 future will **'likely begin in the coming days'**, but admitted he remains in the dark about where he'll be racing next year — his fate tied up in decisions across the wider Red Bull driver pool, which also includes ongoing speculation about whether Verstappen himself will exercise an exit clause from Red Bull.
key_points: Lawson called 2026 **'by far'** Racing Bulls' strongest season under the current rules.
He has scored points in **all but three races** so far this season.
Rookie teammate **Arvid Lindblad** is on a **six-race points streak**.
Lawson says talks on his **2027 future** will 'likely begin in the coming days' — but he doesn't know the outcome yet.

depth.background: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand driver racing for Racing Bulls, Red Bull's sister/junior F1 team, after a brief, difficult stint racing for the senior Red Bull team was cut short. Red Bull runs two connected teams and regularly moves drivers between them based on performance, meaning a driver's next contract is often an internal management decision as much as a results-based one. F1's mid-season **'silly season'** is the informal window when teams sort out next year's driver line-ups, and Lawson's situation is entangled with wider uncertainty over **Max Verstappen's** own future at the senior Red Bull team.

stories.title: The Hundred 2026: Trent Rockets confirm the men's top seed as London Spirit and Birmingham Phoenix are eliminated
stories.what_happened: With most sides having played **six of their eight** group matches, **Trent Rockets** sit atop The Hundred men's table with **20 points from five wins**, the best record of any team this season. Two teams — **London Spirit** and **Birmingham Phoenix** — have already been mathematically eliminated from playoff contention, unable to reach the top three even with wins in their remaining games. The battle for the second and third playoff spots, which go into the **eliminator match at The Oval on August 14**, remains open among the rest of the field. The group winner advances directly to the **final at Lord's on August 16**. In the parallel women's competition, **Trent Rockets** and **Southern Brave** currently lead the table.
key_points: **Trent Rockets** lead the men's Hundred table with **20 points from five wins** in six matches, the best record in the competition.
**London Spirit** and **Birmingham Phoenix** are already **mathematically eliminated** from playoff contention.
Every team has now played **six of eight** group matches, with the table tightening for the remaining top-three spots.
The top-placed team advances straight to the **final at Lord's on August 16**; second and third meet in the **eliminator on August 14**.
In the women's competition, **Trent Rockets** and **Southern Brave** currently lead their own table.

depth.background: The Hundred splits its men's and women's competitions into a single eight-team table each, with every side playing eight group games before the top three advance to the knockouts. Because it's a short, compressed schedule, results pile up fast and teams can be mathematically eliminated well before the group stage technically ends — as has now happened to two of this year's men's sides. Trent Rockets have been the standout team of the men's competition so far, building a lead that puts them in pole position for a direct spot in the final.

stories.title: Ex-FIA steward Johnny Herbert defends stewards after Hamilton vents over penalty streak
stories.what_happened: Hamilton picked up penalties in three consecutive race weekends this season: a five-second penalty for a false start at Silverstone (which the FIA later agreed to reconsider after his protest), a five-second penalty for a first-lap collision with George Russell at Spa-Francorchamps, and at the Hungarian Grand Prix both a three-place grid drop for 'unnecessarily impeding' Oscar Piastri in qualifying and a further five-second penalty for exceeding the pit-lane speed limit by just **0.1 km/h** during a Virtual Safety Car period. Former F1 driver and ex-FIA steward Johnny Herbert publicly defended the stewards' office in response to Hamilton's frustration, saying: 'You can't say it was just bad luck. You can't and mustn't penalise a driver simply because you might not like him. That's not how it works,' and adding that the pit-lane infraction 'was Hamilton's fault, full stop. You can't blame anyone else.'
key_points: **Lewis Hamilton** has picked up **four penalties** across three race weekends — Silverstone, Spa, and Hungary.
At the **Hungarian GP**, Hamilton got a grid drop for impeding Piastri in qualifying plus a penalty for exceeding the pit-lane speed limit by just **0.1 km/h**.
Former steward **Johnny Herbert** defended the officials, saying you 'can't and mustn't penalise a driver simply because you might not like him.'
Herbert called the pit-lane infraction **'Hamilton's fault, full stop'** — no one else to blame.
The friction comes as F1 enters its **summer break**, before racing resumes at Zandvoort on August 21-23.

depth.background: F1 stewards are independent officials — often former drivers, like Herbert — who review incidents each race weekend and can hand out time penalties, grid drops, or reprimands for rule breaches. Drivers regularly push back publicly when they feel penalties are inconsistent, a friction that can shape how future marginal calls are perceived. Hamilton, now driving for Ferrari, has openly criticized officials before.

stories.title: Dangerous heat and nearly 100 uncontained wildfires grip the US West as a punishing weekend heat wave peaks
stories.what_happened: A dangerous heat wave settled over large parts of the US this weekend, sending the heat index to **95°F in New York City**, **101°F in Washington, D.C.**, and **109°F on the New Jersey Shore** on Friday, with a heat advisory in effect from Connecticut to Maryland through Saturday evening. At the same time, the West is battling near-record heat and fire danger: forecasters flagged possible Sunday record highs of **107°F in Madera, California**, **100°F in Denver** and **99°F in Albuquerque**. Nearly **100 large, uncontained wildfires** are currently burning in the region, including 26 in Oregon and 19 in Washington state, and California's Bug Fire broke out Saturday, adding a new blaze to an already stretched firefighting effort. Forecasters warned that wind gusts up to 35 mph combined with humidity as low as 5% would keep creating dangerous fire-spread conditions into the evening.
key_points: Nearly **100 large, uncontained wildfires** are burning across the western US, including **26 in Oregon** and **19 in Washington**
Heat index hit **109°F on the New Jersey Shore** and **101°F in Washington, D.C.** over the weekend
Possible record highs Sunday include **107°F in Madera, California** and **100°F in Denver**
California's **Bug Fire** ignited Saturday, adding to an already-stretched firefighting effort
Wind gusts up to **35 mph** and humidity as low as **5%** are fueling fast fire spread

depth.background: Late-summer heat domes — large, stubborn zones of high pressure that trap hot air in place — have become a near-annual feature across the US West, arriving after a dry spring that leaves grass and brush primed to burn. This year's pattern is unusual for stretching coast to coast: the same window has brought extreme, humid heat to the Northeast via moisture pulled up from the Gulf, alongside the dry heat driving fire risk out West.

stories.title: Galle Gallants win their first-ever Lanka Premier League title, beating Jaffna Kings in a low-scoring final
stories.what_happened: Jaffna Kings batted first in the day-night final and were bowled out for just 123, with Charith Asalanka and Eshan Malinga taking three wickets apiece to dismantle their batting line-up. Galle Gallants then chased the target down comfortably, reaching 126 for 5 in 15.5 overs to seal a 5-wicket win and, with it, their first LPL championship.
key_points: Galle Gallants chased down **123** in just **15.5 overs**, winning by **5 wickets** with 25 balls to spare.
It's Galle's **maiden LPL title** in the tournament's history.
**Charith Asalanka (3/20) and Eshan Malinga (3/25)** dismantled Jaffna's batting to restrict them to just 123 all out.
The final was played under lights at **R. Premadasa Stadium, Colombo**.
Jaffna Kings had looked in strong form, having crushed Colombo Kaps in the **Eliminator** to reach this final.

depth.background: The Lanka Premier League (LPL) is Sri Lanka's marquee T20 franchise cricket tournament, similar in format to India's IPL. Jaffna Kings are a multiple-time strong LPL side who had earned their final spot by beating Colombo Kaps in the Eliminator — the knockout playoff match we previously reported on.

thread.previously: We reported that Jaffna Kings had reached the LPL final, while Colombo Kaps eliminated Kandy Royals in the Eliminator.
thread.changed: Jaffna lost the final itself — bowled out for 123 — as Galle Gallants chased it down to win their first-ever LPL title.

stories.title: Devdutt Padikkal's unbeaten 142 drags India level with Sri Lanka XI on Day 2 of their tour warm-up
stories.what_happened: India lost Yashasvi Jaiswal for a two-ball duck in the very first over, caught behind off pacer Vishwa Fernando. From there, Padikkal anchored a recovery, eventually finishing the day unbeaten on 142 off 164 balls, with KL Rahul (50) and Ravindra Jadeja (63, before retiring hurt) both contributing supporting partnerships. Play was briefly interrupted by rain early in the day. India closed on 357 for 6, just 6 runs short of Sri Lanka XI's declared first-innings total of 363 for 8.

India closed on **357/6**, just **6 runs behind** Sri Lanka XI's first-innings total of 363/8 declared.
**Yashasvi Jaiswal** was dismissed for a **two-ball duck**, caught behind in the very first over.
**Ravindra Jadeja (63, retired hurt)** and **KL Rahul (50)** both chipped in as India recovered from the early setback.
The match's final day is **Sunday, August 9**, with India expected to focus on bowling practice rather than chasing a result.

depth.background: This three-day fixture against a Sri Lanka Cricket XI is an unofficial tour warm-up match, not a Test — it lets India's squad find form and fitness before their official Test series in Sri Lanka begins. We previously reported Padikkal's maiden century anchoring India's fightback on Day 1; this is him extending that same innings into Day 2. A strong showing here strengthens his case for a place in India's Test XI at No. 3.

stories.title: Yemen's army launches a multi-front counter-operation against the Houthis after the Marib massacre
stories.what_happened: On Saturday, August 8, Yemen's armed forces launched what they called a **multi-front operation** against Houthi military positions and equipment across Marib and Hadhramaut provinces, deploying along several axes of contact simultaneously. Army spokesman Col. Majid al-Nuzaili said the action was carried out in direct response to Friday's Houthi missile-and-drone assault on **Sahn al-Jinn camp**, which killed **17 soldiers and officers** and wounded others. The Defence Ministry framed the operation as demonstrating unified command across the armed forces, explicitly stating that an attack on any one front would be treated as an attack on all of them. The army also warned that it would respond to any further Houthi escalation with **decisive military measures**, a sharp change in tone after years in which large-scale fighting between the two sides had largely subsided.
key_points: Yemen's internationally recognised army struck Houthi positions on **multiple fronts** across Marib and Hadhramaut provinces on **Saturday**
It's the direct response to Friday's Houthi missile-and-drone strike that killed **17 government soldiers** at Sahn al-Jinn camp
Army spokesman Col. **Majid al-Nuzaili** said the operation hit Houthi "elements and military equipment" along contact lines
The military declared an attack on **one front is an attack on all fronts**, signalling a unified, coordinated response
It warned it would meet any further Houthi escalation with "**decisive military measures**", raising fears of a return to full-scale war

depth.background: Yemen's civil war has run since **2014**, pitting the Houthis — an Iran-aligned armed movement that controls the capital Sanaa and the north — against Yemen's internationally recognised government, backed militarily and financially by **Saudi Arabia**. A UN-brokered truce mostly held for several years, cooling the front lines even as talks over a permanent peace deal repeatedly stalled. That calm has been unravelling in 2026: Houthi attacks on government-held territory have picked up sharply, and this week's strike on **Sahn al-Jinn** — a major base north of Marib city — was the deadliest single hit on government forces in a long stretch.

thread.previously: On Friday, August 7, Houthi missile and drone strikes on Sahn al-Jinn camp near Marib killed 17 Saudi-backed government soldiers — the concrete escalation Saudi officials had warned was coming.
thread.changed: Yemen's army has now hit back with a multi-front counter-operation against Houthi positions across Marib and Hadhramaut, and warned it will meet any further attack with 'decisive military measures' — the clearest sign yet that both sides are trading blows, not just absorbing them.

stories.title: Russian drones kill a grandmother, grandfather and their 3-year-old grandson in a Kyiv-region strike
stories.what_happened: Overnight into **August 8-9**, Russian drones struck the **Brovary district** just outside Kyiv, destroying a family home and killing a **grandmother, grandfather, and their 3-year-old grandson**. Ukrainian officials reported **4 people killed** in total across the Kyiv capital region as air defenses again failed to intercept the full wave of incoming drones and missiles. This was the **second major Russian attack on the Kyiv region within 48 hours**, coming just days after an August 5 barrage that killed 17 people and wounded 44 using a mix of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and over 100 drones. Officials and residents describe air-raid sirens and interceptions becoming a nightly routine as autumn approaches with no ceasefire in sight.
key_points: Multiple Russian drones destroyed a house in **Brovary**, a Kyiv-region suburb, killing **three generations of one family** overnight
Ukrainian officials say **4 people died** and dozens more were hurt across Kyiv and the surrounding region in the latest barrage
It is the **second major Russian attack on the capital region in 48 hours**, following a bigger strike on August 5 that killed 17
Moscow continues to exploit Ukraine's **shortage of Patriot interceptors** — the only system that can down Russia's ballistic missiles
The strike lands even as Iran-adjacent diplomacy dominates headlines, underlining that the **Ukraine war has not paused**

depth.background: Russia has kept up near-nightly missile and drone barrages against Kyiv through the summer of **2026**, mixing cheap decoy drones with expensive jet-powered models and ballistic missiles designed to overwhelm Ukraine's thinning air-defense umbrella. Ukraine's most effective shield against ballistic missiles is the US-made **Patriot system**, but supplies of interceptors have run critically low as Western stockpiles are stretched across multiple conflicts. Just three days before this strike, a bigger barrage on **August 5** killed 17 people in the same Kyiv region, using 24 ballistic missiles, several hypersonic Zircon or Oniks missiles, and 115 drones.

stories.title: The Hundred's playoff race hits a decisive Saturday as group games near their end
stories.what_happened: Saturday, August 8 brings two of the tournament's more consequential remaining group games: Southern Brave face Manchester Super Giants at the Utilita Bowl, and MI London host Trent Rockets at The Oval, with women's matches at 2:30 PM and men's matches at 6 PM local time. With London Spirit already eliminated from the men's competition after a defeat earlier in the week, the remaining teams are jostling for the two qualification routes — direct entry to the August 16 Lord's final for whoever finishes top of their table after the group stage, or a place in the August 14 eliminator at The Oval for the second- and third-placed sides. Trent Rockets currently lead the men's table, while Southern Brave lead the women's.
key_points: Saturday's fixtures — **Southern Brave vs Manchester Super Giants** and **MI London vs Trent Rockets** — carry direct weight for qualification.
Table-toppers in the men's and women's competitions go **straight to the final** at Lord's on **August 16**.
Second and third-placed teams meet in an **eliminator at The Oval on August 14** for the other final spot.
**London Spirit** are already eliminated from the men's competition after Wednesday's results.
**Trent Rockets** and **Southern Brave** currently lead the men's and women's tables respectively.

depth.background: The Hundred is England cricket's short-form franchise competition, played in 100-ball innings rather than the usual 120, running each August across eight men's and women's teams. Each team plays a round-robin group stage; the format rewards being top of the table since only the top side gets a guaranteed final spot, while second and third have to win an extra eliminator match to get there. Both the men's and women's finals are held at Lord's, English cricket's most famous ground.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi takes his 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' student campaign into BJP-ruled Uttar Pradesh for the first time
stories.what_happened: On **August 8**, Rahul Gandhi held his third 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' event, drawing thousands of young people to KP Ground in Prayagraj — the first time the campaign has entered Uttar Pradesh. The event nearly didn't happen: the management of the host Kayasth Pathshala college initially withdrew permission for the venue, before that cancellation was reversed and the programme went ahead. Gandhi's message centred on examination paper leaks, high coaching fees, and the lack of jobs for educated young Indians — the same grievances that have fuelled ongoing protests elsewhere in the country. The BJP pushed back on the event's significance, with a party spokesperson arguing turnout fell short of comparable events by rival groups.
key_points: **Thousands of students** turned out in Prayagraj for Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's **third 'Chhatron Ki Goonj'** event
It is the campaign's **first stop in BJP-ruled Uttar Pradesh**, after earlier legs in Rajasthan and Uttarakhand
The campaign spotlights **exam paper leaks**, coaching fees, and joblessness among India's youth
The **KP Ground** venue was nearly cancelled after the host college withdrew permission, then reinstated it
BJP dismissed the turnout as underwhelming compared to a rival student event

depth.background: As **Leader of the Opposition** in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi has been running a nationwide student-outreach drive under the banner 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' ("the voice of students"), aimed at channeling anger over exam-paper leaks, rising coaching costs and scarce jobs into a political movement. The campaign began with a mass rally in Rajasthan's Kota, a hub for India's competitive-exam coaching industry, then moved to Dehradun in Uttarakhand, where Gandhi met families affected by alleged exam irregularities. Sunday's stop in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, is significant because UP is both India's most politically important state and a **BJP stronghold**, making it Congress's most direct test yet of whether this youth-grievance message can cut through there.

stories.title: F1 boss Stefano Domenicali says a German Grand Prix return will 'definitely happen', with Hockenheim in early talks
stories.what_happened: On the Q2 2026 earnings call, Domenicali said: **"Germany, for the first time, we are reconnecting with the possibility of having contact with the Hockenheim people to see if, in the future, mid-term, not short-term, they can have a race back."** He confirmed the sport's calendar is fully booked through **2028**, so any German return is realistically a **2029-or-later** prospect, and pointed to the Barcelona-Spa rotation as the likely structural model. The comments came alongside Liberty Media's Q2 results, which showed F1 revenue fell **38% to $764 million** and operating income dropped **61%**, largely because **four fewer races** were held after Bahrain and Saudi Arabia were postponed due to the Middle East conflict. Domenicali linked the German push to the country being the home base of major F1 partners and manufacturers, saying F1 wants Germany to again be one of its most important markets.
key_points: On Liberty Media's **Q2 2026** earnings call, F1 CEO **Stefano Domenicali** confirmed Hockenheim has reopened contact about rejoining the calendar.
He said a German GP return will **"definitely happen"** — but not before **2029**, since the F1 calendar is already locked through 2028.
The likely model is a **rotating slot**, the same cost-sharing format Barcelona and Spa-Francorchamps adopt from 2027, alternating years.
Germany hasn't hosted a points-paying **German Grand Prix** since **2019**; a 2020 Nürburgring race filled a pandemic gap but wasn't badged as the German GP.
Domenicali tied the push to Germany being home to major F1 sponsors and manufacturers, calling it a market F1 wants to matter in again like **"20 years ago."**

depth.background: Germany was once a fixture of the F1 calendar, hosting legends like **Michael Schumacher** and **Sebastian Vettel** at Hockenheim and the Nürburgring for decades, but the race disappeared after **2019** as local promoters struggled to match the hosting fees F1 could command from newer markets. Since then F1 has expanded aggressively into the Middle East, the US (Miami, Las Vegas) and other high-paying destinations, often at the expense of legacy European rounds. The **Barcelona–Spa rotation deal**, under which the two circuits alternate hosting years from 2027, set a new template: a way for classic tracks to stay on the calendar without either side paying for a race every single year. That template is now being floated as the way Germany could get back on the schedule.

stories.title: Devdutt Padikkal's maiden ton anchors India's fightback in Sri Lanka tour warm-up
stories.what_happened: Sri Lanka Cricket XI batted first in the tour match at Colombo's Nondescripts Cricket Club Ground and declared their first innings on **363 for 8**. In India's reply, the top order lost early wickets, but opening batter **Devdutt Padikkal** built a substantial innings, reaching an unbeaten **133** by the second day's close, while Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel were both dismissed cheaply in the middle order. Ravindra Jadeja and the tail continued to support Padikkal as India worked to close the gap on Sri Lanka's total heading into the final day of the fixture on August 9.
key_points: **Devdutt Padikkal** scored an unbeaten **133** in India's reply to Sri Lanka Cricket XI's total.
Sri Lanka Cricket XI had declared on **363 for 8** in their first innings.
India lost quick wickets including **Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel** cheaply in reply.
The tour match at Colombo's **Nondescripts Cricket Club Ground** runs August 7–9.
It's India's final warm-up before the **two-match Test series against Sri Lanka starts August 15** in Galle.

depth.background: India are touring Sri Lanka for a two-match Test series starting August 15 in Galle, with Shubman Gill leading the squad after regular quicks like Jasprit Bumrah were ruled out through injury. This tour match against Sri Lanka Cricket XI — a first-class strength side rather than the full national team — is India's last chance to get batters and bowlers match-fit on Sri Lankan pitches, which typically offer more spin and lower bounce than conditions back home, before the series that actually counts begins.

stories.title: India presses Meta to curb deepfakes, questions whether its algorithm still counts as a neutral 'intermediary'
stories.what_happened: India's **Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY)** held technical talks with Meta's global team over two days, wrapping up around **August 7-8, 2026**. The government formally asked Meta to overhaul its content-recommendation algorithms, submit a detailed **roadmap to curb deepfakes and AI-generated propaganda**, respond faster to government takedown requests, comply with India's data-localisation rules, and tighten moderation of child sexual abuse material and unlabelled synthetic content. Separately, officials are examining a deeper legal question: whether Meta's recommendation system — which actively decides **'what to show to whom'** rather than passively hosting content — still fits the legal definition of a neutral **'intermediary'** under India's IT Rules. Government sources say Meta acknowledged gaps in its current systems during the talks and outlined technical measures it could adopt going forward. No final regulatory decision has been announced yet.
key_points: India's IT Ministry (**MeitY**) held two days of talks with Meta's global team, concluding around **August 7-8**.
Government asked Meta to revamp its recommendation algorithm, submit a **compliance roadmap on deepfakes**, and act faster on takedown requests.
Officials are examining whether Meta's algorithm — which actively decides what to show each user — still qualifies for **'intermediary' legal protection**.
Losing that status could make Meta **directly liable** for deepfakes and misinformation spread on Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp.
Meta reportedly **acknowledged gaps** in its systems and outlined technical measures during the talks.

depth.background: Under India's IT Rules, platforms like Meta get **'intermediary' status** — legal immunity from being sued over what users post — as long as they take down illegal content when flagged. That protection assumes the platform is a neutral pipe, not an active curator. AI-generated **deepfakes** (fake but realistic videos, images or audio) have become a fast-growing problem globally, used for scams, political disinformation, and harassment, and India has been tightening rules around synthetic media and platform accountability over the past year.

stories.title: Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause is now active after a rough first half of 2026
stories.what_happened: Formula 1 hit its **summer break** after the Belgian Grand Prix with Max Verstappen sitting **sixth** in the drivers' championship, more than **100 points** behind runaway leader Andrea Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes. Because his Red Bull contract includes a clause allowing him to leave at the end of 2026 if he's not inside the **top two** in the standings at this point in the season, that exit clause is now formally active. Red Bull has responded by putting a **new contract offer** on the table that would extend Verstappen through **2029** and remove any exit-route language, though it has been under discussion for 'several weeks' without resolution. Verstappen himself downplayed the situation, saying 'there is nothing going on' and that he's focused on getting the most out of the current car, while his manager Raymond Vermeulen said Verstappen 'wants to finish his time with Red Bull' and fulfill his existing deal through 2028.
key_points: Verstappen's Red Bull contract has a **performance clause** letting him leave at the end of 2026
The clause triggers if he's **outside the top two** in the standings at the summer break — which he now is
He heads into the break **sixth**, over **100 points** behind championship leader Antonelli
Red Bull has offered a new deal extending him to **2029** with the exit language removed
Verstappen says '**there is nothing going on**' from his side; his manager says he wants to fulfill his contract to 2028

depth.background: Max Verstappen has driven for Red Bull since 2016 and won four consecutive drivers' championships between 2021 and 2024, making him the most successful driver on the current grid. His existing contract, signed during Red Bull's dominant years, included a **performance-linked exit clause** — a protection for a top driver against being stuck at a team that stops winning. Red Bull's 2026 season has been difficult by its own recent standards, with rivals like Mercedes' Andrea Kimi Antonelli emerging as the dominant force this year. Verstappen's manager, Raymond Vermeulen, has repeatedly said Verstappen intends to honor his contract through 2028, even as rumors persist about interest from rival teams.

stories.title: Ferrari faces a Hamilton-or-Leclerc choice as an ex-engineer says Leclerc looks 'lost' next to his title-chasing teammate
stories.what_happened: With Hamilton holding a 31-point championship lead over Leclerc after the first half of the 2026 season, former Ferrari race engineer Rob Smedley said publicly that Leclerc has looked "lost" this year alongside his more experienced teammate. Smedley argued Ferrari might have to prioritise Hamilton explicitly — potentially through team orders — if it wants a genuine shot at winning the 2026 drivers' championship. The comments came even though Leclerc delivered an emotional victory at the British Grand Prix at Silverstone, his first win since 2024 and Ferrari's landmark 250th grand prix win. Not everyone agrees with Smedley's read: other F1 insiders, including former team principal Otmar Szafnauer, have publicly urged Ferrari to "leave Charles Leclerc alone" rather than subordinate him to Hamilton.
key_points: Hamilton sits **second** in the drivers' championship, **31 points clear** of teammate Charles Leclerc
Former Ferrari race engineer **Rob Smedley** says Leclerc has looked "lost" alongside Hamilton this season
Smedley argues Ferrari may need explicit **team orders favouring Hamilton** to have a real shot at the title
The debate comes despite Leclerc's **emotional British GP win** — his first since 2024 and Ferrari's **250th** race win
Other insiders, including Otmar Szafnauer, say Ferrari should instead **"leave Leclerc alone"**

depth.background: Lewis Hamilton joined Ferrari for the 2025 season chasing an elusive eighth world title after leaving Mercedes, while Charles Leclerc has been Ferrari's talisman driver for years without ever winning a championship himself. Any explicit team decision to favour one over the other — known in F1 as **team orders** — is always sensitive, since it can affect driver morale, sponsor perception, and how fans view the team's fairness.

stories.title: McLaren flags Ferrari's head start on F1's new Madrid circuit after a surprise filming day
stories.what_happened: Ferrari used one of its allotted filming days in July to become the first team to lap the new Madring circuit with Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc behind the wheel, while the venue was still partly under construction. McLaren team principal Andrea Stella said on August 8 that his team was not informed Ferrari had arranged this session, and acknowledged Ferrari may have picked up a genuine, if small, data advantage ahead of the circuit's competitive debut. Hamilton and Leclerc have both downplayed the significance, describing the surface as dusty and low-grip, more like a construction site than a usable racing line. Stella said he expects any edge Ferrari gained to disappear within a few laps once every team runs the circuit properly during the actual race weekend in September.
key_points: Ferrari ran Hamilton and Leclerc on the new **Madring circuit** in a July filming day McLaren says it wasn't told about.
McLaren boss **Andrea Stella** admits Ferrari may have gained **"a little bit of an advantage"** from the early data.
Hamilton and Leclerc have **downplayed** the advantage, calling track conditions "dusty" with little grip.
Stella expects any edge to **fade quickly** once all teams complete proper laps at the venue.
The Madring hosts F1's **Spanish Grand Prix for the first time** this September.

depth.background: The Madring is a brand-new street-style circuit in Madrid that will host the Spanish Grand Prix for the first time in September, replacing the long-time host Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya on the calendar. F1's technical regulations allow teams a limited number of promotional "filming days" each year, where cars run on non-competition tyres for marketing content rather than genuine testing — but any laps a team gets, even on a demonstration run, can still yield useful data on a brand-new, unfamiliar track.

stories.title: India's forex reserves jump a record $10.5 billion in a week to $692.9 billion, as the RBI leans harder on NRI deposits to defend the rupee
stories.what_happened: RBI data released on Friday, August 7, showed India's foreign exchange reserves rose by $10.512 billion in the week ended July 31, taking the total to $692.866 billion — the sharpest one-week increase since the week ended January 30, and the highest reserve level in nearly three months. Foreign currency assets, the dollar, euro and other hard-currency holdings that make up the bulk of reserves, rose $8.75 billion to $564.68 billion, while gold reserves climbed $1.685 billion to $104.743 billion, reflecting both fresh accumulation and higher gold prices. Special Drawing Rights (a reserve asset allotted by the IMF) and India's reserve position with the IMF each ticked up slightly as well. Much of the jump traces back to the RBI's FCNR(B) swap scheme, through which Indian banks had pulled in $36.7 billion in NRI dollar deposits by July 31, drawn in by the RBI absorbing banks' currency-hedging costs so they can offer NRIs better returns than they'd get elsewhere. Analysts expect reserves to cross the $700 billion mark in the coming weeks if the pace of inflows holds, though some caution the rupee itself may see only limited relief from the buffer alone.
key_points: Reserves rose **$10.512 billion in a single week** (ended July 31) to **$692.866 billion** — the **biggest weekly jump since January 30** and a near-**three-month high**.
Most of the gain came from **foreign currency assets**, up **$8.75 billion to $564.68 billion**; **gold reserves** added another **$1.685 billion**, reaching **$104.743 billion**.

The surge is largely traced to Indian banks mobilising **$36.7 billion** through **FCNR(B) deposits** — a scheme that pays Non-Resident Indians attractive dollar-deposit rates, pulling those dollars into the country.
It comes as the **rupee** has fallen roughly **12% over the past year** and hit a **record low near ₹96/$** in May 2026, forcing the RBI to keep intervening to slow the slide.
Governor **Sanjay Malhotra** says reserves remain adequate by standard measures: over **10 months of import cover** and **90.8% external-debt cover**.

depth.background: Foreign exchange reserves are the stockpile of US dollars, gold, and other hard assets a country's central bank holds — used to pay for imports, service foreign debt, and step in to support the local currency when it's under pressure. India's rupee has been under sustained pressure through 2026 from global dollar strength and persistent capital outflows, and it touched a record low against the dollar in May. To defend the currency without simply burning through its existing dollar stockpile, the RBI has been running a scheme to pull in fresh foreign currency: a swap facility that makes it cheaper for banks to offer high-interest FCNR(B) deposit accounts to Non-Resident Indians, in exchange for their dollars flowing into India's reserves.

stories.title: Red Bull's Ford power unit gives it a 'key advantage' in the hunt for a first 2026 win, despite longest winless start since 2015
stories.what_happened: With the 2026 season past its early rounds, Red Bull remains **winless**, its longest drought to start a season since **2015**. But analysts and rivals increasingly point to the **Red Bull-Ford power unit** as a genuine strength rather than a liability, in contrast to pre-season fears about a first-year in-house engine. Max Verstappen has come closest to a win with **two second-place finishes**, including a near-miss chasing down Mercedes' George Russell at the **Austrian Grand Prix** in June. Red Bull's design chief has outlined a path to turning that power-unit strength into wins, but the team still trails Mercedes, Ferrari and McLaren on overall pace. One specific obstacle: rival manufacturers Mercedes and Ferrari are receiving extra engine-development allowances (**ADUO** tokens) under F1's catch-up rules that Red Bull, as a newer engine manufacturer, isn't getting to the same degree.
key_points: Red Bull is the only top team **yet to win a race** in the 2026 season — its **longest winless start** since 2015
Analysts say the new **Red Bull-Ford power unit** has emerged as a genuinely competitive engine under F1's 2026 rules
Max Verstappen has come closest with **two second-place finishes**, including nearly catching Mercedes' George Russell in Austria
Red Bull still trails **Mercedes, Ferrari and McLaren** on outright pace, but engine development gains are closing part of that gap
A lack of extra engine-development tokens (the **ADUO** allowance) that rivals Mercedes and Ferrari are getting remains Red Bull's biggest obstacle

depth.background: F1's 2026 regulations brought a complete rules overhaul — new lighter cars and, crucially, new power-unit rules that reset the engine competition after years of Mercedes dominance in that department. Red Bull split from Honda after 2025 and built its own engine in partnership with Ford, a first-of-its-kind project for the team. Early in the season that engine was seen as a risk, but results through the first several rounds suggest it's holding up better than expected — even though the car and team still haven't converted that into an actual race win.

stories.title: Assam's flood death toll climbs to 98 as monsoon disasters spread beyond Kerala and Himachal
stories.what_happened: Assam's flood death toll rose to **98** as of August 8, according to state disaster officials, making it one of the deadliest flood events in the state this monsoon season. Cachar district has suffered the most deaths at **22**, followed by Sivasagar (10), Karimganj (9), and Golaghat (6), with further casualties in Dhemaji, Nagaon, Udalguri, Sonitpur and Karbi Anglong districts. More than **6.5 lakh (650,000) people** have been affected. Separately, lightning strikes killed at least **14 people** across multiple Jharkhand districts, most of them farm workers caught in open fields. Scientists note the paradox driving this: Assam is facing severe floods even with a **30% rainfall deficit** for the season, because a few short, extremely intense rain bursts — rather than steady rainfall — are overwhelming rivers and drainage.
key_points: Assam's flood death toll has reached **98**, with Cachar district hit hardest at **22 deaths**
Sivasagar (10), Karimganj (9) and Golaghat (6) are among the other worst-hit districts
Separately, at least **14 people** were killed by lightning strikes across Jharkhand
Assam is flooding despite a **30% rainfall deficit** — short, intense bursts are driving the damage
India's monsoon deaths have now passed **100** nationwide since July across multiple states

depth.background: India's June-to-September monsoon is the country's main annual rainy season and usually a lifeline for farming — but 2026's monsoon has been unusually erratic, swinging between dry spells and sudden, intense downpours. This is on top of floods already devastating Kerala and landslide risk shutting the Amarnath Yatra pilgrimage route in Jammu & Kashmir. Assam, in India's northeast, sits on the Brahmaputra river system and floods almost every monsoon, but this year's flooding is notable because it's happening despite the state receiving **less** rain than normal overall.

stories.title: Bangladesh collapse for 54 as Australia XI thrash them by an innings in Test tour warm-up
stories.what_happened: Bangladesh's tour warm-up against a Cricket Australia XI ended in a heavy defeat, losing by an **innings and 38 runs** after collapsing for just **54 runs** in their second innings. The touring side resumed the final morning already two wickets down and were dismissed inside 17 overs before lunch, undone chiefly by Australia XI bowler **Thompson**, who took **8 wickets for 25 runs**. The result is a worrying sign for Bangladesh's batting depth against Australian conditions just days out from the first proper Test of their tour, which starts on August 13.
key_points: Bangladesh were bowled out for just **54** in their second innings of the tour warm-up match.
Cricket Australia XI seamer **Thompson took 8 wickets for 25 runs**.
Bangladesh lost by an **innings and 38 runs**, collapsing inside 17 overs on the final morning.
The result comes just days before Bangladesh's proper **Test series in Australia begins on August 13**.
Bangladesh started the day **two wickets down** and never recovered momentum.

depth.background: Bangladesh are touring Australia for a two-Test series starting August 13, and this three-day warm-up fixture against a Cricket Australia XI (a second-string state/domestic representative side, not the full national team) was meant to help the visitors acclimatise to Australian pitches and conditions before the real series begins. Warm-up matches like this are typically used by touring sides to fine-tune batting techniques against faster, bouncier pitches than what teams face at home, and by hosts to test fringe domestic bowlers against international-standard batting.

stories.title: Jasprit Bumrah ruled out of India's Sri Lanka Tests as uncapped J&K pacer Auqib Nabi gets his maiden call-up
stories.what_happened: India confirmed that Jasprit Bumrah will miss the upcoming two-Test series in Sri Lanka because he has not recovered from a left knee niggle picked up during the second ODI against England in Cardiff last month — an extension of fitness issues that have dogged him since this year's T20 World Cup. In his place, India have called up Auqib Nabi, a 29-year-old seamer from Jammu & Kashmir, for his first-ever senior national call-up. Nabi arrives in form, having taken 104 wickets across the last two Ranji Trophy seasons, including 60 wickets in 2025-26 as J&K won its maiden Ranji Trophy title, and he already has recent experience in Sri Lankan conditions from an India A tour. The first Test begins in Galle on August 15, followed by the second in Colombo.
key_points: **Jasprit Bumrah** is out of India's two-Test series in Sri Lanka with an ongoing **left knee niggle**
**Auqib Nabi**, a 29-year-old Jammu & Kashmir pacer, earns his **maiden India call-up** as his replacement
Nabi took **104 wickets** across the last two Ranji Trophy seasons, including **60** in J&K's title-winning 2025-26 campaign
Bumrah's issue traces back to a **Cardiff ODI** against England last month, extending problems since the **T20 World Cup**
The first Test starts in **Galle on August 15**, with the second following in Colombo

depth.background: Bumrah, widely regarded as the world's best fast bowler, has battled recurring back and knee issues over the past two years, forcing India to carefully manage how much cricket he plays, particularly in the longer Test format. His absence for this tour puts extra weight on India's seam bowling attack, and opens a door for uncapped domestic performers — like Nabi, who has been in career-best form for Jammu & Kashmir and was also part of an India A squad that recently toured Sri Lanka, taking six wickets in two first-class matches there.

stories.title: India bars new solar and wind projects within 1km of its borders on security grounds
stories.what_happened: India's Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has issued formal guidelines prohibiting any **new solar, wind or hybrid renewable energy project within 1 kilometre** of the Line of Control (LoC) with Pakistan, the Line of Actual Control (LAC) with China, or the International Border. Projects proposed within **50 km** of these borders will now require security clearance from the MHA, and those within **20 km** will separately need a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Defence. The guidelines also bar engaging engineers, staff or labour from land-border countries — specifically naming **Pakistan, Bangladesh and China** — without explicit central government permission. Developers must route every application through the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, which forwards it, along with the state government's land-allotment approval and the project's exact coordinates, to the MHA and Defence Ministry for clearance.
key_points: MHA guidelines ban new solar, wind and hybrid renewable projects within **1 km** of the LoC, LAC and International Border.
Projects within **50 km** of these borders now need **Home Ministry security clearance**.
Projects within **20 km** additionally need a **No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Defence**.
Engineers, staff and labour from **Pakistan, Bangladesh and China** are barred from these projects without central government permission.
All applications must route through the **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy**, which forwards them for security clearance.

depth.background: India has been rapidly expanding solar and wind capacity in its border states — Gujarat, Rajasthan, Punjab and Ladakh among them — as part of its renewable-energy push, and much of the best wind and solar resource sits precisely in these sparsely populated frontier regions. That proximity to sensitive, militarily strategic borders has increasingly worried security planners, especially given large-scale infrastructure projects can require foreign contractors, equipment and sometimes foreign labour. The Ministry of Home Affairs' Internal Security wing, which handles border-security policy, drew up these guidelines to close that gap between the renewable-energy build-out and border-security vetting.

stories.title: Jharkhand's exam-scam protest escalates: a hunger striker is hospitalised as students prepare to gherao the state Assembly
stories.what_happened: The protest, which began around July 25-29, hit its 13th and 14th days on August 6 and 7 with the situation intensifying rather than cooling. Six protesters had been on hunger strike, and on August 7 one of them, Rahul Kranti — fasting since the night of August 4 — was rushed to Ranchi Sadar Hospital after his health worsened; Leader of Opposition Babulal Marandi visited him there. The same day, Chief Minister Hemant Soren publicly reached out to the agitating students for the first time, saying the government was ready for dialogue and committed to reforms, while Parliamentary Affairs Minister Radhakrishna Kishore announced a four-minister committee to monitor the protests. Students, in turn, finalised an 11-member delegation — eight student representatives, a lawyer and two technical experts — to negotiate with the government. Despite Jharkhand's CID arresting 11 people connected to the alleged leak, including a suspected 'mastermind,' protesters say they don't trust a state-run investigation and are holding firm on their demand for an outside CBI or retired-judges probe. With no resolution reached, students have announced they will gherao the Jharkhand Legislative Assembly on August 10 if their demands remain unmet.
key_points: The protest has entered its **14th day**, with student leader **Devendra Nath Mahto** on hunger strike since **August 3** demanding Chief Minister **Hemant Soren's** resignation.
Protester **Rahul Kranti** was **hospitalised on August 7** after his health deteriorated during the fast; five other students remain on hunger strike.
Students want the **14th JPSC exam** cancelled and re-held, plus an **independent CBI or judicial probe** — they've rejected the state's own **CID investigation** as untrustworthy.
Jharkhand's **CID** has already arrested **11 people**, including alleged 'mastermind' Suman Saurav, but that hasn't satisfied protesters.
Students plan to **gherao (surround and blockade) the state Assembly on August 10** if demands aren't met; CM Soren has now offered talks and formed a 4-minister panel to monitor the crisis.

depth.background: In July, aspirants preparing for Jharkhand's 14th Public Service Commission (JPSC) civil-services exam and the JSSC-CGL recruitment test alleged the papers had been leaked and results rigged, after screenshots of an answer sheet went viral appearing to show candidates who had failed still making the merit list. Under the banner of the 'JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch,' job aspirants began an indefinite sit-in at Ranchi's Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in late July. The movement has drawn direct inspiration from Delhi's recent 'Cockroach Janta Party' protests over the leaked NEET-UG medical entrance exam, which forced the Union Education Minister to resign — activist Sonam Wangchuk, who fasted 26 days over that issue, has personally called Jharkhand's hunger strikers. In a state where a government exam can be a once-in-a-generation shot at economic security, allegations that the process itself was rigged cut especially deep.

stories.title: Aston Martin's Adrian Newey says he's confident of keeping Fernando Alonso beyond 2026
stories.what_happened: Aston Martin team boss **Adrian Newey** said he believes the team will 'continue our relationship' with Fernando Alonso beyond the current season, even though Alonso is out of contract at year's end and has said he'll make a decision on his F1 future during the summer break. The team has had a difficult 2026, scoring just **one point** across the first 11 grand prix weekends, with both the Newey-designed AMR26 chassis and Aston Martin's Honda power unit underperforming. There were signs of progress at the **Hungarian Grand Prix**, where a **16-part car upgrade** helped Alonso reach Q2 (the second qualifying segment) for the first time all season, with Alonso and teammate Lance Stroll finishing 13th and 14th in the race. Honda is preparing a further engine update to arrive at the **Dutch Grand Prix**, the first race after the summer break, which the team hopes will build on the Hungary upgrade's momentum.
key_points: Newey says Aston Martin will '**continue our relationship**' with Alonso past 2026
Alonso, a **two-time world champion**, is out of contract at season's end and will decide **during the summer break**
Aston Martin has scored just **one point** across the first 11 race weekends this season
A **16-part upgrade** at the Hungarian GP got Alonso into Q2 for the first time all year
Honda is bringing a further engine update at the **Dutch Grand Prix** when the break ends

depth.background: Fernando Alonso is one of F1's most experienced drivers, a two-time world champion (2005, 2006) who joined Aston Martin in 2023 partly on the promise that legendary designer **Adrian Newey** — architect of championship-winning cars for Red Bull, Williams and McLaren — would eventually build the team into a title contender. Aston Martin's 2026 season has instead been its worst in years, scoring almost no points, which has raised questions about whether Alonso, now in his 40s, would stay with a struggling team or look elsewhere for a final shot at competing at the front. Newey's AMR26 car and Honda's new power unit have both underperformed relative to expectations for the new engine and technical-regulation cycle that began this season.

stories.title: India threatens to strip Meta of its legal 'safe harbour' shield as a Modi-video takedown widens into a probe of its algorithms
stories.what_happened: On **August 5–6**, Meta's global affairs chief Joel Kaplan and other executives met Union IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and the parliamentary panel in Delhi. Kaplan apologised for the 'error restricting PM Modi's post,' but the committee had already set a **three-day deadline** demanding a personal apology from Zuckerberg and action against whoever ordered the takedown, warning that safe harbour would otherwise be reviewed. During the same meetings, Indian officials separately raised concerns that Meta's ad-review systems had let through **child sexual abuse material** in paid Instagram promotions, and pressed the company on deepfakes and unlabelled synthetic content. By **August 8**, the government had escalated the scrutiny further: it is now formally examining whether Meta's algorithm-driven 'recommendation system' — which decides what each user sees — means the company is actively curating content like a publisher, rather than passively hosting it like a true intermediary. Officials say they will review the outcome of this week's engagements with Meta before deciding whether to seek a formal legal opinion on withdrawing the protection.
key_points: A parliamentary panel gave Meta a **three-day ultimatum** to have CEO **Mark Zuckerberg personally apologise** over the brief removal of a PM Modi video, or risk losing its legal 'safe harbour' protection.
Meta's global affairs chief **Joel Kaplan apologised** to IT minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on **August 5**, calling the takedown 'an error' — but Meta hasn't confirmed Zuckerberg himself apologised.

The government has now widened the fight: it is examining whether Meta's **recommendation algorithms** make it a 'publisher' rather than a neutral 'intermediary' — a distinction that could strip its legal immunity entirely.
Officials also pressed Meta's global team in Delhi on **deepfakes, child sexual abuse material (CSAM), and unlabelled AI-generated content** during in-person talks this week.
Losing safe harbour would make Meta legally liable for everything users post on Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp — platforms used by **hundreds of millions of Indians** every day.

depth.background: 'Safe harbour' is the legal shield under **Section 79 of India's IT Act** that protects platforms like Meta, Google and X from being sued or prosecuted over content their users post — as long as the platform acts as a neutral 'intermediary' and takes down unlawful material when asked. The protection is the entire legal foundation social media runs on in India: without it, a platform could be held directly responsible for every post, video or message on its network. The current fight began after Meta briefly restricted a **July 23 Facebook video** in which PM Modi addressed students during protests over exam-paper leaks; Meta called it a technical error, but a **Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communications and IT**, chaired by BJP MP Nishikant Dubey, called the removal 'an attack on democracy' and refused to accept a glitch as an explanation.

stories.title: Toto Wolff hits back at 'whinging' Ferrari with a pointed engine claim
stories.what_happened: In comments published today, Toto Wolff countered what he characterized as Ferrari 'whinging' about rivals with a pointed claim about engine performance, continuing a public feud that started when Ferrari's Fred Vasseur accused Mercedes and Red Bull of effectively cheating by developing their power units faster than the rules should allow. Wolff has repeatedly questioned in recent weeks how Ferrari can afford its aggressive stream of upgrade packages — including a second major package introduced at Barcelona in June — while staying under F1's cost cap, suggesting Ferrari must be 'running out of money soon.' Vasseur fired back that Wolff's framing was hypocritical: when Mercedes or Red Bull push hard on development they're praised as geniuses, but when Ferrari does the same, it's branded cheating.
key_points: Mercedes boss **Toto Wolff** pushed back on Ferrari's complaints about rivals' engines, calling out what he frames as Ferrari **'whinging'**.
The spat traces back to Ferrari team principal **Fred Vasseur** accusing Mercedes and Red Bull of 'cheating' over engine development pace.
Wolff has separately questioned how Ferrari affords its **near-constant upgrade packages** within F1's cost cap.
Vasseur countered that it's 'ironic' — when Mercedes or Red Bull develop fast, they're called geniuses; when Ferrari does, it's called cheating.
The row comes as all four top teams jostle for advantage under F1's **all-new 2026 engine and chassis rules**.

depth.background: 2026 introduced Formula 1's biggest rules overhaul in years — new, lighter, more electrically-powered engines and revised aerodynamics, designed to close the field up. That reset has scrambled the usual pecking order: Mercedes, Ferrari, Red Bull and others are all still finding performance mid-season, which has fueled unusually public sniping between team bosses about who is developing fastest and whether everyone is playing by the same cost-cap rules. Wolff and Vasseur have clashed before, but the tone has sharpened as the championship fight tightens.

stories.title: Audi shuts the door on Carlos Sainz for 2027 as Williams counters with a $30M deal to keep him
stories.what_happened: With Williams languishing 9th in the constructors' standings (just **11 points from 11 races**) and Sainz saying his own title hopes have been 'delayed by a year or two,' rumors grew that he could move to Audi for 2027 — helped by his family's Audi ties and his prior working relationship with Binotto. Reports say Williams responded with an offer worth roughly **$30 million a year**, plus performance bonuses, to keep him through the next two seasons. Binotto has now publicly closed that door, telling RacingNews365 he is **'very happy'** with his current lineup of Nico Hülkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto, meaning any Sainz-Audi reunion would have to wait until at least 2028. Sainz has since confirmed both Audi and Alpine are off the table for him, leaving him tied to Williams for now.
key_points: Audi boss Mattia Binotto says he's **'very happy'** with Hülkenberg and Bortoleto through 2027
That rules out a Sainz-Binotto reunion at Audi until at least **2028**
Williams has reportedly offered Sainz roughly **$30 million a year** plus bonuses to stay
Williams currently sits **9th** in the constructors' championship with just 11 points from 11 races
Sainz says both the Audi and Alpine options are now off the table for him

depth.background: Carlos Sainz is a four-time grand prix winner who left Ferrari for Williams in 2025 to help rebuild the once-dominant, now-struggling team. Audi entered F1 in 2026 as a full manufacturer team, built from the former Sauber squad, with **Mattia Binotto** — Sainz's old boss from his Ferrari days — running it. Every mid-season, F1's driver market ('silly season') sees teams and drivers jostling over who lines up where the following year; this year Williams' poor form fueled speculation Sainz might jump ship.

stories.title: Super Typhoon Dolphin, a storm meteorologists call unprecedented, slams Okinawa and barrels toward Shanghai
stories.what_happened: Typhoon Dolphin made landfall in **Japan's Okinawa and Kagoshima prefectures on Saturday, August 8**, injuring **six people** (mostly elderly residents who fell in high winds) and knocking out power to more than **50,000 buildings** combined. Sustained winds reached **162 km/h** with gusts to **216 km/h**, prompting **ANA and JAL to cancel flights** to Okinawa. The storm is now forecast to make landfall on **China's coast between Zhejiang and northern Fujian provinces** sometime between the afternoon of **August 9** and the morning of **August 10**. **Shanghai has issued a blue typhoon alert and evacuated more than 30,000 residents** from at-risk areas, while authorities have suspended ferry routes, construction work, and fishing along the coast. Forecasters warn eastern Zhejiang could see over **600mm of rain** — enough to cause serious flooding. The Philippines is also seeing heavy monsoon rain, intensified by the typhoon's outer bands, across Metro Manila and 23 provinces.
key_points: Typhoon Dolphin exploded from a tropical storm to a **Category 5-equivalent super typhoon in just 24 hours** — something China's weather bureau says has **never been recorded before**.
It hit Japan's **Okinawa and Kagoshima** on Saturday, injuring **six people** and cutting power to over **50,000 buildings**.
Sustained winds reached **162 km/h**, with gusts up to **216 km/h**; peak winds over open water hit **234 km/h**.
China expects landfall between **Zhejiang and northern Fujian** on **Aug 9-10** and has evacuated over **30,000 people** from Shanghai's risk zones.
Eastern Zhejiang could see over **600mm of rain**; ferries, construction, and fishing have been suspended along the coast.

depth.background: Typhoons are the Pacific's version of hurricanes, and they typically take several days to build strength as they cross warm ocean water. Dolphin formed on **July 27 near the International Date Line** and then intensified explosively — going from a tropical storm to a top-tier super typhoon in roughly a day, a speed China's National Meteorological Center calls **unprecedented in recorded history**. It is now tracking toward one of the world's most economically important coastlines: the **Shanghai region**, a hub for shipping, manufacturing, and finance.

stories.title: India's Sai Sudharsan ruled out of Sri Lanka Test series with a toe stress fracture, reopening the No. 3 battle
stories.what_happened: The BCCI has ruled Sai Sudharsan out of India's upcoming two-Test tour of Sri Lanka due to a **stress reaction/fracture in his right big toe**, originally suffered during India A's tour of Sri Lanka in July 2026 — a tour where he'd scored **132, 7 not out, 168, and 25 not out**, underlining how well he was playing before the injury. He has been rehabbing at the **BCCI Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru**, and the team's sports science staff say he's progressing but needs more time for the bone to heal, so he did not travel with the squad. With his No. 3 spot open, **Devdutt Padikkal** — who scored a century in a warm-up match — is now the frontrunner to fill that batting position, while for the squad slot itself, **Sarfaraz Khan** is reported as the likely replacement, with **Shaik Rasheed** and **Ruturaj Gaikwad** also floated as options. No final BCCI squad confirmation has been made yet. The two Tests are scheduled for **August 15 in Galle** and **August 23 in Colombo**.
key_points: **B. Sai Sudharsan**, India's first-choice Test No. 3 batter, is out of the two-Test Sri Lanka tour with a **stress fracture in his right big toe**.
The injury happened during India A's July tour of Sri Lanka, where he'd scored **132, 7*, 168 and 25*** — showing exactly how in-form he was.
He's been rehabbing at the **BCCI Centre of Excellence** in Bengaluru and did not travel with the squad.
**Sarfaraz Khan** is the reported frontrunner to replace him, with **Shaik Rasheed** and **Ruturaj Gaikwad** also in the mix.
The two Tests start **August 15 in Galle** and **August 23 in Colombo** — India already lost pace bowler **Jasprit Bumrah** to injury for this tour.

depth.background: Sudharsan is a young left-handed batter who had recently locked down India's **Test No. 3 spot** — a high-pressure position in the batting order historically filled by greats like **Rahul Dravid** and **Cheteshwar Pujara**. Losing him now, on top of already missing frontline pace bowler **Jasprit Bumrah** for the same tour, compounds a run of pre-series personnel setbacks for India heading into Sri Lanka.

stories.title: Kerala's flood toll climbs to 28 as over 40,000 remain in relief camps
stories.what_happened: Kerala's flood-related death toll has climbed to **28** as of August 8, up from the 20 reported a day earlier, with **over 40,000 people** now sheltering in relief camps across the state. The state government said the rains and flooding have damaged crops across **3,264 hectares** belonging to **36,829 farmers**, with total losses estimated at **₹99.29 crore**, and it has formally sought **₹110 crore** in financial assistance from the central government to cover the damage. Authorities have declared a holiday for educational institutions in eight districts — Thrissur, Pathanamthitta, Kozhikode, Kottayam, Wayanad, Kannur, Kasaragod and Alappuzha — as an Orange Alert remains in force for seven districts today.
key_points: Kerala's flood death toll has risen to **28**, up from 20 just a day earlier.
More than **40,000 people** remain in relief camps across the state.
Crop damage is estimated at **₹99.29 crore**, hitting **36,829 farmers** across 3,264 hectares.
The state has asked the Centre for **₹110 crore** in financial assistance.
Schools are shut in **8 districts** including Kottayam, Wayanad and Alappuzha as an Orange Alert continues in 7 districts.

depth.background: Kerala's southwest monsoon has been unusually intense this year, with repeated spells of heavy-to-extremely-heavy rain triggering flooding and landslides across the state's hilly and low-lying districts. India's Meteorological Department (IMD) has cycled through red and orange alerts for different districts through late July and early August as successive rain bands moved through. Kerala is especially exposed because its terrain combines steep, landslide-prone Western Ghats hill districts with low-lying backwater and coastal areas that flood quickly once rivers and lakes fill up.

thread.previously: As of August 7, we reported Kerala's monsoon flood death toll at 20, with the IMD issuing a fresh red alert for seven districts and continuing heavy rain.
thread.changed: The death toll has risen to 28, over 40,000 people are now in relief camps, and the state has quantified the damage: ₹99.29 crore in crop losses across nearly 37,000 farmers, prompting a ₹110 crore request for central assistance.
